title: Theorem B: enough forms
line: A second moment shows a few translates span
summary: A Petersson-type second moment, with Bessel functions and unfolding, shows a few translates span almost all target forms.
story: `Spanning` proves Theorem B with a second-moment argument: the moments (`SecondMoment`), equal multiplicities (`Multiplicities`), measures and Bessel functions (`Bessel`), unfolding (`Unfolding`), a main term and the remaining terms.
Its conclusion is that a few translates of the normalised Poincaré map span almost all of the target forms.

elsewhere.label: Tam Nguyen Duc: Bessel and seesaw (original edition; matched by title)

modules.title: Functions of positive type and singular minors
modules.group: The second moment and the spanning theorem
modules.note:
A function `Θ` on a finite group `G` is of positive type if `Θ (a⁻¹ * b) = ⟪u a, u b⟫` for some
vectors `u a` of a complex inner product space.

Notions from other files:

* `New.invTransposeGL` is the automorphism `g ↦ (gᵀ)⁻¹` of `GL n R`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.card_mul_sum_det_eq_zero_le`: let `k` be a field with `q` elements, `π` a representation by
  `n × n` matrices over `k`, `A₀` and `A₁` two `n × m` matrices and `Θ ≥ 0` of positive type.
  Suppose that, for `v ≠ 0`, the stabilisers of `A₀ v` under `π` and of `A₁ v` under the
  contragredient of `π` have `Θ`-mass at most `Y ≥ 0`. Then the set where `det (A₁ᵀ π(s) A₀)`
  vanishes has mass at most `(2 Θ(G) + q ^ (|m| + |n| / 2) Y) / q`. The proof counts the kernel with
  an additive character and uses Cauchy–Schwarz.

modules.title: Few translates fill
modules.group: The second moment and the spanning theorem
modules.note:
Let a finite group act unitarily on `T`, let `pr₀` be the projection onto a stable subspace `T₀`,
and let `B : S → T` be linear. Suppose that `pr₀ B` is almost an isometry from below in mean square
and that the second moment of the operators `B* s B` is nearly as small as Cauchy–Schwarz allows.
Then a few translates `s pr₀ B` span almost all of `T₀`. In this file `‖A‖`, written of a linear map
`A`, is its Hilbert–Schmidt norm.

* `New.hilbertSchmidtNorm`, `New.IsNearIsometry`: the Hilbert–Schmidt norm, and the first
  hypothesis.
* `New.isSpread_of_second_moment`: for any subspace `W` of `T₀`, the preimage of `W` under some
  translate `s pr₀ B` is small, in terms of the share of `W` in `T₀` (`New.IsSpread`).
* `New.IsSpread.exists_few_le_finrank_iSup_range`: a logarithm times `dim T₀ / dim S` translates
  span almost all of `T₀`.
modules.literature:
Rank bounds from second moments: Welch 1974. Greedy covering with a logarithmic loss: Wolsey, Greedy
algorithm for the submodular set covering problem, 1982.

modules.title: The dimension of the target and one good translate of the Poincaré map
modules.group: The second moment and the spanning theorem
modules.note:
For admissible data `D`, the finite group `Ḡ = D.chosenGL` acts on the forms on `Y₀`, and `e₀`
projects them onto the target `D.targetForms`, the good forms, of dimension `D.targetDim`. The
source `D.SourceForm` is the space of the forms that the Poincaré map `P = D.poincare` sends to
forms on `Y₀`. This file supplies the hypotheses of the lemma on one translate,
`New.isSpread_of_second_moment`, for `P` and draws its conclusion. The spanning theorem itself,
`New.Data.enough_forms`, is deduced in `New.Reduction.ShortAndEnough`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.targetDim_le_card_mul_besselDegree_mul_mass`: the target has dimension at most
  `#Ḡ · deg · mass_r`. It is counted on the definite space `D.spaceW D.m`, where the level is free.
* `New.Data.hasAmplitudeBlocks_scaledPoincare`: the blocks of `P* s P`, once `P` is scaled
  (`New.Data.scaledPoincare`).
* `New.Data.bad_types_rare`: `e₀` is a product of two central idempotents, one for each level prime,
  and their complements have a small coefficient at `1`.
* `New.Data.isNearIsometry_e₀_comp_scaledPoincare`,
  `New.Data.targetDim_mul_sum_hilbertSchmidtNorm_sq_le`: the two hypotheses of the lemma on one
  translate.
* `New.Data.isSpread_goodPoincare`: for every space of target forms, with share `α` of the
  dimension, some translate `s e₀ P` has a preimage of dimension at most about `(1 + α) / 2` times
  the dimension of the source.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.filling`: the data `New.Filling` attached to `D`: the level `N`, the two level primes
  with their chosen places, and Bessel systems chosen from `New.Data.exists_besselSystem`.
* `New.Filling.besselDegree`: the product `deg` of the formal degrees at the infinite places.
* `New.mass`: the mass `mass_r` of the genus of the standard lattice of rank `r`.
* `New.Data.paramW`: twice the parameter `New.Data.targetParameter`, indexed by the basis of `Y₀`.
* `New.Data.RowIndex`: the index set of the basis of `Y₀`.
modules.literature:
For every space `F` of target forms, with share `α` of the dimension, some translate `s e₀ P` has
rank modulo `F` at least nearly `(1 - α) / 2` times the dimension of the source. Spanning by
Poincaré series and the link between least second moment and tight frames are known in the
literature. Related work: Petersson, Über die Entwicklungskoeffizienten der automorphen Formen,
1932; Benedetto–Fickus, Finite normalized tight frames, 2003; Muić, Spectral decomposition of
compactly supported Poincaré series and existence of cusp forms, 2010.

modules.title: Spherical Hecke operators away from the level, and eigensystems
modules.note:
The level `M` is the product of the primes `D.levelPrime 0`, `D.levelPrime 1`, and `D.chosenPlace`
runs through the chosen places above it. The spherical Hecke operators away from `M` form an algebra
that acts at once on the forms `D.principalForms V` of principal level for all hermitian spaces `V`.
It commutes with the finite group `D.chosenGL`, so it acts on the good forms `D.goodForms V`, the
image of the idempotent `D.e₀`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.sphericalAlgebra`, `New.Data.heckeAlgebra`: the spherical elements of the group algebra
  and the operators that they give; `New.Data.heckeOnGood` is the action on good forms.
* `New.Data.heckeOperator`: the operators `T_{w,i}` at the places `New.Data.IsSplitOffLevel`, as
  members of the Hecke algebra; `New.Data.principalHeckeSplit` is the operator on one space.
* `New.Data.eigenPart`: the part with a given eigensystem. The parts are independent
  (`New.Data.iSupIndep_eigenPart`), and in finite dimension they span the forms
  (`New.Data.iSup_eigenPart_eq_top`).
* `New.Data.exists_hecke_proj_eigenPart`: a Hecke operator that is `1` on one part and `0` on
  finitely many others.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.principalForms`: the forms on `V` of archimedean type `typeKernel D.paramW s` that are
  fixed by the principal level `J_M = D.chosenLevel` at the chosen places; `V.formRep` is the
  action of the finite adelic unitary group `G_f = Gf E n` on forms, and `K₀ = stdLevel E n` is its
  standard maximal compact subgroup.
* `New.heckeSplit`: the Hecke operator `T_{w,i}` at a split place `w`, of the double coset of
  `diag (ϖ 1_i, 1)`.
* `New.universalLevelAlgebra`: the elements of a group algebra that keep the vectors of a given
  level in every representation.

modules.title: Equality of multiplicities
modules.note:
The spaces `Y_0, W_1, …, W_m` share the group `G_fin`, the level and the parameter, and differ only
in their signs at the real places. Let `V`, `V'` be two hermitian spaces for whose signs the
parameter `New.Data.paramW` has gap `D.gap`. Then a spherical Hecke operator away from the level `M`
has the same trace on their good forms. The equality of traces is deduced from the comparison of
traces for a test function that is cuspidal at one split place (`New.trace_eq_of_isCuspidalAt`).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.exists_heckeAlgebra_eq_mul_inner_of_hasSum_rallisTerm`: the sums of scalar multiples of
  the Rallis series on two spaces are the same multiples of matrix coefficients of one element of
  the Hecke algebra.
* `New.Data.trace_heckeOnGood_eq`, `New.Data.charpoly_heckeOnGood_eq`,
  `New.Data.det_heckeOnGood_eq`: equal traces, characteristic polynomials and determinants.
* `New.Data.rallisOnGood`, `New.Data.det_rallisOnGood_eq`: the Rallis series preserves the good
  forms and has the same determinant on the good forms of both spaces.
* `New.Data.finrank_goodForms_inf_eigenPart_eq`: each eigensystem has the same multiplicity.
* `New.Data.targetDim_eq_finrank_goodForms_spaceW`: the good forms on `Y_0` and on `W_j` have the
  same dimension.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.principalForms`: the forms fixed by the principal level `D.chosenLevel` at the chosen
  places above `M`.
* `New.Data.principalRep`: the action on them of `D.chosenGL = ∏ GL_r(𝔽_w)`, over the chosen places
  w.
* `New.Data.goodForms`: the image of the idempotent `D.e₀` on these forms.
* `New.Data.heckeAlgebra`, `New.Data.eigenPart`: the spherical Hecke operators away from `M`, and
  the part with a given eigensystem.
* `New.HCParam.HasGap`: entries of the parameter with different signs are at least `h` apart.
modules.literature:
The equality of traces is the analogue of the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence for a quaternion
algebra that is ramified exactly at the real places. Related work: Harris–Labesse, Conditional base
change for unitary groups, 2004; Labesse, Changement de base CM et séries discrètes, 2011.

modules.title: Bessel systems at a real place: length and norm bounds, lattice basis, discriminant
modules.note:
The file sets up the objects that connect the analysis at one real place with the filling argument.
`New.Shape.G₁` is the unitary group of a hermitian form made of ϱ hyperbolic planes, a positive
space X₀ with basis κ and a vector z with h(z, z) = −1. The frame is (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z). The Bessel
subgroup `New.Shape.Form.besselS` is generated by the unipotent group 𝖴 = `New.Shape.Form.besselU`
and by `New.Shape.Form.besselH` = U(X₀). `New.frameVector y a` is the image under `y⁻¹` of the
`a`-th frame vector. The file first proves elementary bounds on the length `New.besselLength y`, the
infimum of `‖s * y‖ + 1` over `s` in `besselS`. It then defines the lattice basis, the discriminant
𝗀 and the link, and the structure `New.BesselSystem` listing what is used of a Bessel function W and
its cut W♭. Norms on G₁ are those of the Euclidean norm for which the basis e_a, x_i, z, e*_a is
orthonormal. The frame has n = ϱ + 1 vectors.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.norm_add_one_le_of_mem_frameBox`: `‖y‖` is bounded by the lengths of `y⁻¹ e_a`, `y⁻¹ z` and
  `y⁻¹ e*_a`.
* `New.orthoFrame`, `New.gramSchmidtMatrix`: Gram–Schmidt for the frame. The orthogonal vectors are
  left invariant under `besselS` (`New.orthoFrame_besselS_mul`), and the Bessel length bounds their
  lengths on both sides (`New.norm_orthoFrame_mem_Icc`). The triangular matrix depends continuously
  on the point (`New.continuous_gramSchmidtMatrix`).
* `New.besselLength_le_of_norm_orthoFrame`: conversely, these lengths bound `besselLength y`; the
  proof corrects `y` on the left until the first bound applies. `New.besselLength_le_of_dual` is the
  case of a frame with a bounded triangular dual system.
* `New.besselLatticeBasis`: the basis of the lattice, in which `x_{k₀}` is replaced by
  `v = x_{k₀} / p̄ + z / N`. `New.gram_besselLatticeBasis` gives its Gram matrix, with middle block
  `New.latticeMiddleGram`.
* `New.frameDisc`: the quantity `|D_{ϱ+1}|² - N² |D_ϱ|²` in the leading minors `New.leadingMinor`,
  written `𝗀`. Up to sign it is the Gram determinant of the frame and its image under an isometry
  (`New.det_gram_framePair`).
* `New.IsCutPair`: the L² bounds of W and W♭, the support of W♭, and decay below a common integrable
  majorant (`New.IsDecayMajorant`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.besselFrame`: The indices of the frame (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z) among the basis indices.
* `New.Shape.middleGram`: for a scalar N, the diagonal matrix on κ plus one point, with entries 1 on
  κ and −N at the extra point.
modules.literature:
References on Bessel functions and kernels are in `New.Spanning.Bessel.FillingData`; references on
the decay of discrete series coefficients are in `New.Spanning.Bessel.CutTailBound`.

modules.title: The Gram section γ_Z of the frame Gram matrix map on the unitary group G₁
modules.note:
For `γ` in the unitary group `New.Shape.G₁`, let `Z(γ) = New.realFrameGram γ = Fᴴ J₁ γ F` be the
matrix of products of the frame `F = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)` with its translate by `γ`. Let
`Ω = New.Shape.openCell` be the open set of invertible `Z` for which `ξ(Z) = invCorner Z`, the last
diagonal entry of `Z⁻¹`, has absolute value less than `1`. The file writes down an explicit matrix
`γ_Z` for `Z ∈ Ω` and proves that it is real differentiable with polynomial bounds.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.RealPlace.sectionMatrix`: a matrix in two variables `Z`, `W`, equal to `γ_Z` at `W = Zᴴ`.
* `New.RealPlace.differentiableAt_sectionMatrix`,
  `New.RealPlace.norm_sectionMatrix_le_and_norm_fderiv_le`: the matrix is real differentiable in
  `Z`, with polynomial bounds for it and its derivative.
  `New.RealPlace.IsBoundedInCell.norm_sectionMatrix_le` asks for bounds at the point `Z` only.
* `New.RealPlace.gramSection`: on `Ω` the matrix is an isometry of `J₁`
  (`New.RealPlace.sectionMatrix_isometry`), so it is the matrix of an
  element `γ_Z` of `G₁` (`New.RealPlace.coe_gramSection`).
* `New.RealPlace.measurable_gramSection`: the section is measurable.
* `New.RealPlace.realFrameGram_gramSection`: `Z(γ_Z) = Z` for `Z ∈ Ω`.
* `New.RealPlace.exists_eq_mul_gramSection_mul`: by Witt's theorem, `Z(γ) = Z ∈ Ω` determines `γ` up
  to factors `unipotentOf q * embedH k`, which fix the frame, on both sides.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.BesselIndex`: the index set of the basis `e₁, …, e_ϱ`, `x_k` (`k ∈ κ`), `z`,
  `e*₁, …, e*_ϱ`; `k₀ = New.Shape.k₀` is a distinguished index in `κ`.
* `New.Shape.J₁`: the Gram matrix of the hermitian form defining `G₁`, with `ϱ` hyperbolic pairs
  `e_a, e*_a`, the identity on the span `X₀` of the `x_k` (`k ∈ κ`), and `h(z, z) = -1`.
* `New.Shape.frameCols`, `New.Shape.dualFrameCols`: the matrices `F` and `F'` whose columns are the
  basis vectors `(e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)` and `(e*₁, …, e*_ϱ, x_{k₀})`.
* `New.Shape.FrameMatrix`: the complex `(ϱ+1) × (ϱ+1)` matrices; `New.Shape.top` is the last index.

modules.title: Normalisation of a Bessel function and of its cut
modules.note:
Let `W` be an integrable Bessel function on G₁ whose type is an irreducible representation of the
compact group `U(κ)`. The operator `∫ W ⊗ W^*` over 𝖴∖G₁ commutes with this representation, so it
is a scalar, and its trace is the squared L² norm of `W`.

* `New.BesselSystem.orthonormal`: for the full function of a Bessel system the operator is `1`, so
  its coordinates are orthonormal in L²(𝖴∖G₁).
* `New.IsCutPair.exists_integral_cut_mul_conj_eq`: for the cut function it is a scalar between `0`
  and `1`.
* `New.IsCutPair.lintegral_sq_inner_cut_le`: the upper bound, tested on a vector.

Notions from other files:

* `New.Shape.G₁`: the unitary group G₁ of the complex hermitian form given by a shape; `U(κ)` is
  the unitary group of the standard positive form on the index set κ of the shape, embedded in G₁
  by `New.RealPlace.embedH`.
* `New.besselQuotMeasure`: the measure on G₁ that computes integrals over 𝖴∖G₁, where 𝖴 is the
  unipotent group `New.Shape.Form.besselU`.
* `New.IsBesselFunction`: a bounded measurable function on G₁ that transforms on the left by a
  fixed character under 𝖴 and by a unitary representation, its type, under `U(κ)`.
* `New.IsCutPair`: a Bessel function (`.full`) whose squared L² norm is the dimension of its
  value space, and its cut (`.cut`): a Bessel function that vanishes outside a region of bounded
  size, is close to it in L² and agrees with it where the size is small.
* `New.BesselSystem`: a cut pair of irreducible type, with further bounds.

modules.title: The mean value inequality over the Gram matrix of two frames
modules.note:
Let `G₁` be the real unitary group `New.Shape.G₁`, `e = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)` its frame, `R°` the fixer
of the frame, the product of the unipotent group `𝖴⁰ = New.Shape.Form.besselU0` and the compact
group `H = U(κ)`, and `γ_Z = New.RealPlace.gramSection Z` the section of the map that sends `γ` to
the matrix `Z` of the products of `e` with `γ e`, over the open set `Ω = New.Shape.openCell` of the
invertible `Z` whose inverse has last diagonal entry of absolute value less than `1`.

On the frames `y = γ e` the fibre measure of the Gram map is compared with Haar measure in
`New.LeGramFibre.mconv_fixerHaar_le`. This file bounds the same fibre measure from below, by `dZ`
times a measure on the frames whose products with `e` form the matrix `Z`. Such a frame is `y' Z`
with `y'` dual to `e`. The first `ϱ` vectors of `y'` are moved by `𝖴⁰`, and the part of the last one
in `X₀ = ℂ ^ κ` runs over a sphere.

One can find the measure on the frames over `Z` by letting both frames vary and dividing two
equalities of fibre measures, the one on pairs of frames, which are tuples of `2 (ϱ + 1)` vectors
with an invertible Gram matrix, by the one on frames. Here a fibre measure enters only through the
relation of being at most it (`New.LeFibreMeasure`); the measure over `Z` is computed directly in
coordinates as a lower bound, and the fibre measure on frames is used as an upper bound.

* `New.RealPlace.lintegral_eq_lintegral_sphereMass_mul_dualFrameOfGram`: Lebesgue measure on the
  tuples dual to the frame, in terms of their Gram matrix and of `R°`.
* `New.RealPlace.leGramFibre_gramSectionMeasure`: the law of `s γ_Z e`, with a density proportional
  to `New.RealPlace.gramDiscReal Z ^ (|κ| - 1)`, is at most the fibre measure.
* `New.RealPlace.lintegral_gramSection_le`: the mean value inequality for the integral of
  `f (s' γ_Z s)` over `s, s'` in `R°` and `Z` in `Ω`.

Notions from other files:
* `fixerHaar 𝔰`: the measure `du dh` on `R°`, with `u = unipotentOf q` for Lebesgue measure `dq` and
  `embedH h` for the Haar probability measure `dh` on `U(κ)`.
* `frameCols`, `dualCols`, `isotropicCols`, `definiteCols`, `freeCols`: the matrices with the
  columns `(e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`, `e*_b`, `e_b`, `x_i`, and `(e_b, x_i)` respectively.
* `J₁`: the hermitian form on the space with the basis `e_b, x_i, z, e*_b`, which pairs `e_b` with
  `e*_b`, is the identity on `X₀` and is `-1` at `z`.
* `top`, `k`, `k₀`: the last index of the frame, the number `|κ|` and a chosen element of `κ`.
* `embedH h`: the element of `G₁` that acts by `h` on `X₀` and fixes the other basis vectors.
* `hermOfReal t`: the hermitian matrix with the real coordinates `t`.
modules.literature:
Part of the bound on the open cell for the Bessel integrals at a real place; see
`New.Spanning.Bessel.FillingData`. For fibre measures of the Gram map compare Siegel, Über die
analytische Theorie der quadratischen Formen, Ann. of Math. 36 (1935).

modules.title: Unfolding bounds over G₁ and the L² bound at the section γ_Z via Sobolev
modules.note:
`New.Shape.G₁` is the complex unitary group of the shape `𝔰`, with index set
`New.Shape.BesselIndex`. `𝖴 = New.Shape.Form.besselU` is its Bessel unipotent group, and
`𝖴⁰ = New.Shape.Form.besselU0` is the subgroup of `𝖴` fixing the frame e₁, …, e_ϱ, z; their Haar
measures are `New.Shape.besselHaar` and `New.Shape.besselHaar₀`. An unfolding inequality bounds
suitable integrals over `G₁` by integrals over `𝖴∖G₁`. An `L²` bound on the quotient `𝖴∖G₁` for
convolutions, the hypothesis `New.RealPlace.HasSchurBound`, then gives an `L²` bound on a bounded
part of the orbit of the section `γ_Z = New.RealPlace.gramSection Z`, at the price of a power of a
size bound `P`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.lintegral_mul_le_of_frameMatrix_le`: the unfolding bound on `G₁`.
* `New.RealPlace.HasDerivWords`: families that behave like iterated right derivatives on `G₁`.
* `New.RealPlace.lintegral_gramSection_integral_le`: the bound for the convolution at `γ_Z (u h)⁻¹`,
  integrated over `h ∈ U(κ)` and the `u ∈ 𝖴⁰` with `‖u‖ ≤ P ^ 20`. Sobolev's inequality on a small
  cube at `Z` (`New.sobolev_trace_cube`) replaces the value at `Z` by mean squares of derivatives,
  which are bounded by integrals over `𝖴∖G₁`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.Form.besselS`: the Bessel subgroup, generated by `𝖴` and by the image of `U(κ)` under
  `New.RealPlace.embedH`.
* `New.besselQuotMeasure`: the measure on `G₁` that integrates a `𝖴`-invariant function over
  `𝖴∖G₁`.
* `New.RealPlace.gramDiscReal`: 𝗀(Z) = |det Z|² − |D_ϱ|², D_ϱ the leading principal minor of order
  ϱ. In the coordinates `γ_Z` Haar measure has density at least c_G 𝗀(Z)^{|κ|−1}, with
  c_G = `New.Shape.openCellConst` (`New.RealPlace.lintegral_gramSection_le`).
* `New.realFrameGram`: for y in `G₁`, the matrix of hermitian products of the frame vectors with
  their images under y; it sends `γ_Z` to Z when Z lies in the open cell Ω = `New.Shape.openCell`.
* `New.RealPlace.IsBoundedInCell Z P`: Z lies in Ω, and ‖Z⁻¹‖, ‖Z‖ and (1 − |ξ|²)^{−1/2} are at
  most P, where ξ is the last diagonal entry of Z⁻¹.

modules.title: The group of the Bessel period at a real place
modules.note:
The group `R = U ⋊ H` at one real place, its Haar measure `du dh`, and the integral over `R` that
defines the Bessel function.

Here a shape `𝔰` gives the number of hyperbolic planes and the index set `κ` of the middle block,
`𝔰.G₁` is the unitary group of the hermitian space of that shape, `besselU` (the `U` of
`R = U ⋊ H`) is its block upper unitriangular subgroup, `H` is the image of the unitary group
`U(κ)` under `embedH`, and `besselS` is the Bessel subgroup generated by `besselU` and `H`.

modules.title: Bounds near a point of Ω and the open cell bound for a Bessel system
modules.note:
Write Ω = `New.Shape.openCell`, 𝗀(Z) = |det Z|² − |D_ϱ|² and ν(Z)² = 1 − |ξ|², where ξ is the last
diagonal entry of Z⁻¹. At and near a point `Z` of Ω (so `0 < 𝗀(Z)`) the matrix, its inverse, 𝗀 and ν
obey explicit size bounds. Such bounds on a ball supply the hypothesis of
`New.RealPlace.lintegral_gramSection_integral_le`. For a Bessel system, a family of kernels is then
shown to be an `L²` contraction at each `γ` in `New.Shape.G₁` whose frame Gram matrix lies in Ω,
provided that some `y` and `γ⁻¹ y` both lie in a frame box of large enough size.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.RealPlace.isBoundedInCell_of_inv_le_gramDiscReal`: if `M⁻¹ ≤ 𝗀(Z)` and the entries of `Z` are
  at most `M ^ 2`, a power of `M` bounds the matrix, its inverse and `1 / ν`.
* `New.RealPlace.gramDiscReal_div_two_le_and_isBoundedInCell`: on a small ball about such a `Z` the
  matrix stays in Ω with these bounds, and 𝗀 drops by at most a factor two.
* `New.BesselSystem.exists_isOpenCellBound`: the family of shifted kernels is a contraction from
  `L²(ν)` to `L²(m)`, with `m` a probability measure and `ν` of total mass at most `pairingBoundSq`
  (`New.BesselSystem.IsOpenCellBound`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.RealPlace.gramDiscReal`: 𝗀(Z) = |det Z|² − |D_ϱ|² for a (ϱ+1)×(ϱ+1) complex matrix Z
  (`New.Shape.FrameMatrix`), where D_l (`New.leadingMinor`) is the leading principal minor of order
  l.
* `New.Shape.openCell`: The set of invertible (ϱ+1)×(ϱ+1) complex matrices whose inverse has last
  diagonal entry ξ of absolute value less than 1; `New.RealPlace.oneSubNormSqInvCorner` is
  ν² = 1 − |ξ|².
* `New.RealPlace.gramSection`: For Z in Ω, an element γ_Z of G₁ whose frame Gram matrix
  (`New.realFrameGram`) is Z.
* `New.frameBox`: The set of y in G₁ such that every vector y⁻¹f_a of the moved frame
  (`New.frameVector`) has Euclidean norm at most a given bound.
* `New.besselLength`: For y in G₁, the infimum of ‖sy‖ + 1 over s in the Bessel subgroup S
  (`New.Shape.Form.besselS`).
* `New.BesselSystem 𝔰 B f`: a Bessel function `besselFn .full` on G₁ with values in ℂ^I, its cut

  bounds, the natural number `f` the rate of decay, and |I| / `deg` is the constant of Schur's

modules.title: One pairing on the open cell, at all places together
modules.note:
Let `X` be a finite family of Bessel systems (`New.BesselSystem`), `W` the tensor product of their
Bessel functions and `W♭` that of their cuts. Let `φ` be a function of `z` of modulus at most `1`,
left invariant under the fixers of the frames and not necessarily a product over the places, such
that `φ (z) W♭ (γ z) ⊗ W♭ (z)^*` vanishes outside boxes. The integral of this product is bounded by
the root of the product of the local bounds `New.pairingBoundSq`, plus the integral of `‖φ‖` times
the norm of the difference between the uncut and cut kernels.

The operator bounds of `New.BesselSystem.exists_isOpenCellBound` multiply over the places, and one
shift that is no worse than the mean gives the bound for `W`.

Notions from other files:
* `BesselSystem`: two continuous functions on the group `G₁`, `besselFn .full` and its cut
  `besselFn .cut`, with values in `ℂ^I`, parameters `b` and `f`, and a degree `deg`.
* `frameBox ρ`: the `y` with `‖y⁻¹ f_a‖ ≤ ρ` for every vector `f_a` of the frame; `besselFixer` is
  the subgroup that fixes these vectors.
* `besselLength y`: the infimum of `‖s y‖ + 1` over `s` in the Bessel subgroup.
* `realFrameGram γ`: the matrix of products `h(f_a, γ f_b)` for the hermitian form `h`;
  `gramDiscReal Z` is `|det Z| ^ 2 - |D| ^ 2`, with `D` the leading minor one size smaller.
* `pairingBoundSq γ deg ρ d`: the square of the bound of the open cell at one place, a power of
  `ρ ^ (9 n) / 𝗀` times `d ^ 2 / (deg * openCellConst * (𝗀 / 2) ^ (k - 1))`, where
  `𝗀 = gramDiscReal (realFrameGram γ)`, `n = 𝔰.n` and `k = 𝔰.k`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.BesselSystem.pairKernel`: the matrix of `W (y) ⊗ W (γ⁻¹ y)^*`. Its adjoint is the matrix of
  `W (γ⁻¹ y) ⊗ W (y)^*`, which is `New.BesselSystem.piKernel` at `γ⁻¹`.
* `New.BesselSystem.enorm_integral_pairKernel_cut_le`: compact support and the bound for the pairing
  of the cut functions.

modules.title: Bessel systems of discrete series type and a Bessel function large at a point
modules.note:
Given a unitary frame that diagonalises the form `New.Shape.J₁`,
`New.Filling.IsDiscreteSeriesBessel` ties an abstract Bessel system `New.BesselSystem` to a discrete
series parameter `l` and a weight `kw` of the subgroup `H = U(X₀)`. Let `𝖴` be the unipotent group
`New.Shape.Form.besselU` and let `R = 𝖴 H` be the Bessel group, realised as the subgroup
`New.Shape.besselGraph` of `G₁ × H`. There is a point `x` of bounded size at which the period of a
discrete series coefficient over `R` is large. For a parameter of large gap, the average of the
coefficient over `R` converges absolutely (`integrable_besselIntegrand`). It is a Bessel function
(`isBesselFunction_besselAverage`) that the kernel of the discrete series reproduces
(`convolve_besselAverage`).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.DiscreteSeries.UnitarySignFrame`: a unitary frame taking `J₁` to the diagonal matrix of signs
  `ε`.
* `New.Filling.IsDiscreteSeriesBessel`: the Bessel system has type `(l, kw)`.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.IsSteep.exists_stationary_point`: a point `x` of bounded length at which the
  period over `R` is large. It carries the stationary position of `U(X₀)` to the standard frame.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.G₁`: the unitary group of the complex hermitian form made of ϱ hyperbolic planes, the
  standard positive form on X₀ = ℂ^κ, and one vector z with h(z, z) = −1. Its Gram matrix is
  `splitGram ϱ (middleGram κ 1)`, indexed by `New.Shape.BesselIndex`. Here n = ϱ + 1, k = |κ| and
  r is the dimension of the whole space.
* `New.Shape.besselGraph`: the Bessel group `R = 𝖴 H`, stored as the pairs of an element of G₁ and
  its image in H, with the measure `du dh`.
* `New.simpleRootSum`: the sum of the entries just above the diagonal on the frame e₁, …, e_ϱ, z.
* `New.besselLength`: for y in G₁, the infimum of ‖s y‖ + 1 over s in R; it is the length of y.
* `New.HCParam.HasLargeGap l A`: for `l = 2λ` with N coordinates, the entries are distinct, of the
  parity of N − 1, and entries of `λ` at coordinates of opposite sign are 500 N³ + A apart or more.
modules.literature:
See `New.Appendix.DiscreteSeries.Periods` for related work. See
`Lib.DiscreteSeries.Bessel.UnipotentHaarMeasure` for sources.

modules.title: The Bessel function at a real place: decay and cut
modules.note:
The file concerns Bessel functions (`New.IsBesselFunction`) on the real unitary group
G₁ = `New.Shape.G₁`: bounded functions to ℂ^I that transform on the left by a character of the
unipotent group 𝖴 = `New.Shape.Form.besselU` and by `rep` under H = U(κ). Throughout, p is a unitary
frame that diagonalises the form, c_λ = `New.HCParam.dsCoeffInFrame` is the discrete series
coefficient of a parameter l = 2λ with large gap (`New.HCParam.HasLargeGap`), v is a unit vector of
ℂ^I, and e = deg·c_λ with deg = `New.HCParam.formalDegree`. F is reproduced by e if F * e = F for
the convolution `New.convolve`: (F * e)(y) = ∫ e(a⁻¹) F(ya) da. The measure of 𝖴∖G₁ is
`New.besselQuotMeasure`. G₁ consists of r × r matrices with r = `𝔰.r`, ‖g‖ is the operator norm, and
n = `𝔰.n` = ϱ + 1 with ϱ the number of hyperbolic planes of the form.
* `New.exists_isDecayMajorant_besselAverage`: the normalised average of c_λ over the Bessel subgroup
  decays in the length, below a bounded integrable weight (`New.IsDecayMajorant`).
* `New.besselCut`: the cut of a function at length b^(6n+2); it is close to the function in L²
  (`New.IsDecayMajorant.lintegral_sq_besselCut_sub_le`).
* `New.exists_isCutPair_besselAverage`: a multiple of the average is reproduced by e and forms a cut
  pair (`New.IsCutPair`) with its cut.

Notions from other files:
* `New.besselLength`: for y in G₁, the infimum of ‖sy‖ + 1 over s in the Bessel subgroup S = 𝖴H
  (`New.Shape.Form.besselS`).
* `New.Shape.besselGraph`: the group 𝖴H as a graph, the pairs (g, k) in G₁ × U(κ) with k⁻¹g in 𝖴.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.besselAverage`: the function y ↦ ∫_S c_λ(x⁻¹ s y) π(s)⁻¹ v ds, where π is the
  character on 𝖴 and `rep` on H.
* `New.scaledBesselLength`: the larger of 1 and the length divided by b^(6n).
modules.literature:
A Bessel function at a real place, an average of a discrete series coefficient with a large period
integral, inherits the coefficient's decay. Normalised and multiplied by a scalar cut-off, it gives
a continuous approximant, close in L² and compactly supported modulo the unipotent group, with an
explicit tail bound. Related work: Muić, Fourier coefficients of automorphic forms and integrable
discrete series, 2015; Miličić, Asymptotic behavior of matrix coefficients of the discrete series,
1977; Wallach, Real Reductive Groups II, 1992.

See `New.Spanning.Bessel.FillingData` for related work.

modules.title: Schur's bound for a Bessel function and its derivatives
modules.note:
Let `l = 2λ` be a doubled Harish-Chandra parameter of large gap and `c_λ` the coefficient `dsCoeff`
on `U(diag ε)` of its discrete series; the same letter stands for its pullback
`New.HCParam.dsCoeffInFrame` to `G₁` by the frame. Let `deg` be the formal degree
`New.HCParam.formalDegree`. Write `(F * k) y = ∫ k a⁻¹ • F (y a)` and `e = deg · c_λ`; as
`e a⁻¹ = deg · conj (c_λ a)`, the condition `F * e = F` says that `F` is fixed by the idempotent of
the discrete series. Such a bounded function has right derivatives of all orders, and they are
convolutions with kernels of controlled norm. Schur's bound in `L²(𝖴 ∖ G₁)` follows, `𝖴` being the
unipotent group `besselU`.

Notions from other files:
* `l : New.HCParam ε` is twice a Harish-Chandra parameter; `HasLargeGap A` bounds its gaps below.
* `p : UnitarySignFrame 𝔰 ε` is a unitary frame in which the form of `G₁` is `diag ε`.
* `frameEquiv : G₁ ≃ₜ* U(diag ε)` is conjugation by the frame.
* `Bumps ε` are the smooth compactly supported functions on `U(diag ε)`; `smear f` sends a bump `β`
  to the convolution of the continuous function `f` with `β`.
* `bumpDeriv` is the action of matrices on bumps by differentiation, `adTwist g` precomposes it with
  conjugation by `g`, and `word w` applies the action of the matrix units of the word `w`.
* `New.IsBesselFunction rep F`: `F` is bounded, measurable and transforms by a character under
  `besselU` and by `rep` under `U(κ)`.
* `𝔰.r` is the number of indices `BesselIndex` of `G₁`, and `𝔰.n` is one more than the number of
  hyperbolic planes of the shape `𝔰`.
* `RealPlace.HasSchurBound F rep B C`: `F` has right derivatives of all orders that are again Bessel
  functions, those of order `s ≤ 2 n ^ 2` satisfying Schur's `L²` bound with `B ^ (2 s) C`.
* `besselQuotMeasure` is the measure on `G₁` that represents integration over `besselU ∖ G₁`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Smoothness and Schur's orthogonality relations for vectors of a discrete series
representation (Harish-Chandra).

modules.title: Filling data from admissible data, with Bessel systems at the real places
modules.note:
The filling theorem is stated for abstract data (`New.Filling`). This file builds such data from
admissible data D (`New.Data`). At each real place it constructs a Bessel system of the type fixed
by D. It then assembles these systems, the relevant primes and places, and the level `D.levelX 0`
into the filling data. It identifies that level with the preimage of the level K(M) of
`New.Filling.principalLevel`: here M = p₀ p₁, and K(M) includes a congruence modulo π.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.exists_besselSystem`: the Bessel function at a real place, with its normalisation,
  Schur's bound, decay, cut and local bounds. That its coordinates are orthonormal is
  `New.BesselSystem.orthonormal`, in `New.Spanning.Bessel.Orthonormality`.
* `New.Data.filling`: the prime `New.Data.N`, the primes p₀, p₁ (field `levelPrime`) with their
  chosen places, the level `D.levelX 0` and a Bessel system at each infinite place.
* `New.Data.levelX_zero_eq_comap`: the level `D.levelX 0` is the preimage of the principal
  congruence subgroup K(M), that is `New.Filling.principalLevel`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.piNIdele`: the principal finite idele of `π`, where `N = π π̄`; `New.Data.piNPlaces` is
  the set of places dividing `π`.
* `New.Data.piM`: the conjugate of the integer `D.piMBar` of norm `p₀ p₁`; the chosen places are its
  prime divisors.
modules.literature:
At a real place, integrals of a Bessel function on an indefinite unitary group against its
translates have Fourier transforms decaying beyond a band; the bounds themselves are proved in the
imported files. These integrals replace Petersson's J-Bessel kernel in showing that few translates
almost span the target forms. Rank one is classical, and Bessel kernels are studied for GL(n) and
GSp(4).

Related work: Petersson, Über die Entwicklungskoeffizienten der automorphen Formen, 1932; NIST DLMF
§10.22; Baruch, On Bessel distributions for quasi-split groups, 2001, and Bessel distributions for
GL(3) over the p-adics, 2004; Comtat et al., Effective Kuznetsov trace formula for GSp(4), 2025.

modules.title: The data, standing hypotheses and amplitudes of the filling theorem
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
The data and the vocabulary of the filling theorem. The space is `V` = (`ϱ` hyperbolic
planes) ⊕ `X₀ ⊕ E z`, with `X₀` definite of rank `k = |κ|` and `h(z, z) = -N`. Its Gram matrix is
`New.Shape.Form.splitGram`, its indices are `New.Shape.BesselIndex`, and the frame
`New.Shape.besselFrame` is `(e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`.

* `New.Filling`, `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`: the data with its size hypotheses, and the standing
  hypotheses.
* `New.Filling.G`, `New.Filling.GFin`, `New.Filling.ResidueGL`: `U(V)` over a ring, over the finite
  adeles in the lattice basis, and the product of `GL` over the residue fields of the chosen places.
* `New.Filling.ratToInf`, `New.Filling.ratToFin`, `New.Filling.reduction`: the maps to the infinite
  places (rescaled to `New.Shape.G₁`), to the finite adeles, and reduction.
* `New.Filling.termsOver`, `New.Filling.amplitude`, `New.Filling.amplitudeSum`: the rational terms
  over a block `(c, s, c')`, made of two classes and an element of `ResidueGL`; the amplitude of a
  term; and the sum of the amplitudes over a set `T` of terms. Divided by `unipotentCovolume`, this
  sum is the contribution of `T` to the block. Integrals over the quotients of G_∞ by the groups
  `classUnipotent c` are written with the cutoffs `classCutoff c`.
* `New.Filling.Agrees`, `New.Filling.IsStable`, `New.Filling.termsOfLink`: the elements of
  `ResidueGL` that respect the unipotent character, the stable sets of terms, and the terms of
  nonzero discriminant with a given link.

Letters in the docstrings: 𝖴 = `New.Shape.Form.besselU` is the unipotent group,
𝖴⁰ = `New.Shape.Form.besselU0` is its subgroup fixing the frame, and H is `U(X₀)`. The group
`New.Shape.Form.besselS` is generated by 𝖴 and H. G_∞ is the product of copies of `New.Shape.G₁`
over the infinite places. K = `latticeStabilizer`, K(M) = `principalLevel`, h_c = `classRep c`,
Λ = `frameScaleProd`, and f_0, …, f_ϱ is the frame.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape`: the number ϱ, the index set κ of X₀ and one index k₀ in κ; k = |κ| and n = ϱ + 1.
* `New.BesselSystem`: for the real number b, two continuous functions W (`FullOrCut.full`) and W♭
  (`FullOrCut.cut`) from G₁ to ℂ^I, I a finite index set, that satisfy bounds in b and in a positive
  constant `deg`; they are Bessel functions of an irreducible representation of U(k) on ℂ^I.
* `New.frameDisc`: for Z of size ϱ+1 with leading minors D_l, the quantity |D_{ϱ+1}|² − N²|D_ϱ|²,
  where |x|² means x x̄.

modules.title: Bessel data: level subgroup, Eichler maps and strong approximation for the unipotent group
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
The file works with filling data `S : New.Filling E 𝔰` and the unitary group `S.G` of the form
`T.splitGram`, where `T` is the middle Gram matrix, at rational points, finite adeles and
archimedean points. The middle space is X₀ ⊕ E z, with X₀ spanned by the basis vectors indexed by
`κ`. Write 𝖴 for the Bessel unipotent group `New.Shape.Form.besselU`. Write H for
`New.Shape.Form.besselH`, the unitary group U(X₀), acting only on the basis vectors indexed by `κ`.
Write `New.Shape.Form.besselS` for the group they generate. Write σ = `New.simpleRootSum` for the
sum of the entries just above the diagonal on the frame. The level is `S.M = p₀ p₁` with
`pᵢ = S.levelPrime i`, and `S.chosenPlaces i` are the chosen places of norm `pᵢ`. K(M) is
`S.principalLevel`. For a class c, h_c = `S.classRep c` is its representative in H. For classes c,
d, `S.translateByClassReps c d γ` is h_c⁻¹ γ h_d, and `S.termsOver c s d` is the set of rational γ
with `S.translateByClassReps c d γ` integral of reduction s.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.besselFn_adelicToInf_mul_eq_prod_wave_smul`, `New.Filling.besselFn_ratToInf_mul`: how
  the Bessel function `New.Filling.besselFn` transforms under left translation by `𝖴`.
* `New.exists_mem_besselU_eq_eichlerMap`: for a hermitian invertible form, if x is a combination of
  the frame vectors of index below a and v is orthogonal to these vectors, then the Eichler map
  along x and v, with ς = τ h(v, v), lies in the unipotent group `New.Shape.Form.besselU`; the lemma
  also computes its `New.simpleRootSum`.
* `New.besselU_dense`, `New.Filling.exists_besselU_approx`: strong approximation for 𝖴.
* `New.Filling.mem_reducedImage_besselU_iff_exists_termsOver`,
  `New.Filling.prod_wave_eq_star_unipotentChar`: the rational points of 𝖴 that are integral for a
  class map onto the reduction of the integral points of 𝖴(𝔸_f), and on them the character at
  infinity is the conjugate of the finite character at an integral point with the same reduction.
* `New.Filling.exists_besselS_mem_termsOver`: each reduction `s` of an integral element of
  `New.Shape.Form.besselS` is reached from each class c by a rational element of
  `New.Shape.Form.besselS`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.Form.splitGram`: The Gram matrix of ϱ hyperbolic planes and a middle space with Gram
  matrix T: identity blocks pair the first and last ϱ indices, T is the middle block, all else is
  zero.
* `New.Filling.selfDualChar`: The additive character x ↦ ψ_f(−x/ϖ) of the finite adeles.
* `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`: The standing hypotheses on the data: among them, `sourceLevel` is the
  preimage of K(M), `reduction` is onto, and some size inequalities hold.
* `S.GFin`: The finite adelic points of the unitary group in the lattice basis.
* `New.Filling.unipotentChar`: The value of the additive character `S.selfDualChar` at M⁻¹ σ(u),
  where σ(u) = `New.simpleRootSum u` sums the entries of u at the simple roots.

modules.title: Near terms in the filling theorem: frames, cell ranks, nearness and integrality
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
The terms `γ` of the count in the filling theorem are rational elements of the unitary group.
The data are `S : New.Filling E 𝔰` for a shape `𝔰`, with the size hypotheses
`New.Filling.IsAdmissible`, which compare all constants with powers of the large parameter `b`.
For the frame `(e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`, `New.frameImage γ` is the matrix of its image under `γ`, and
`S.frameProducts γ` is the Gram matrix of the frame against its image, with leading minors
`New.leadingMinor`. This file describes how the flags of the frame and of its image under `γ` meet,
defines the cell rank and nearness of `γ`, proves a norm identity for `S.termDisc γ`, bounds the
Gram entries of near terms by powers of `S.b`, and shows that the Gram entries of terms are
algebraic integers.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.CharsAgree`, `New.PairOccursAt`, `New.Filling.HasCellRank`: the terms that respect
  the unipotent character, the vectors common to the two flags of a term, and its cell rank.
* `New.Filling.IsNear`: `γ` is near if some boxed point `y` (`New.Filling.boxedPoints`) has `γ⁻¹ y`
  boxed.
* `New.Filling.norm_sq_middle_part_eq`, `New.Filling.map_termDisc_eq_norm`: a norm identity, which
  makes `S.termDisc γ` real and nonnegative at every infinite place. So `S.termDisc γ` is totally
  positive or zero (`New.Filling.termDisc_pos_or_eq_zero`).
* `New.Filling.IsNear.norm_frameProducts_le`, `New.Filling.IsNear.norm_map_leadingMinor_sq_le`: for
  a near term, the Gram entries and the leading minors are bounded by powers of the size parameter
  `S.b`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.G`: for a commutative ring R with involution, the unitary group over R of ϱ
  hyperbolic pairs and the middle Gram matrix diag(1, …, 1, −N) on X₀ ⊕ Ez, in the basis e₁, …, e_ϱ;
  x_i (i in κ), z; e*₁, …, e*_ϱ.
* `New.Filling.termDisc`: 𝗀(γ) = |D_{ϱ+1}|² − N²|D_ϱ|², with D_l the leading minors of
  `New.Filling.frameProducts γ`.
* `New.Shape.Form.besselU`, `New.Shape.Form.besselU0`: the Bessel unipotent group 𝖴 of isometries
  that are block upper unitriangular and trivial on the middle block, and its elements that fix each
  vector of the frame.
* `New.Filling.mainSecondMoment`, `New.Filling.identitySecondMoment`: the numbers
  sourceDim² / (besselDegree · mass), with the mass of the genus of the standard lattice, and
  sourceDim times the order of the reduced image of the Bessel subgroup `besselS`.

modules.title: Links of isometries, the link isometry Υ_γ, and invariance under `besselU`
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
Let `γ` be an isometry of the form `T.splitGram`, which is made of `ϱ` hyperbolic planes and a
middle space with Gram matrix `T`. Let `A` be the span of the first `ϱ` basis vectors, and let
`New.frameImage γ` be the image of the frame `(e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`. The link of `γ` is the set of pairs
of middle coordinates of `t` and `γ⁻¹ t`, for `t` orthogonal to `A` and `γ A`.

A filling `S` over a CM field `E` provides a prime `N = S.N`. Its middle space is `X₀ ⊥ E z_N`,
where `X₀` has an orthonormal basis indexed by `𝔰.κ` and `z = z_N` has the norm `-N`. The positive
space `X₀ ⊥ E z⁺` has the same coordinates, and `z⁺` has the norm `N`. After an exchange of the
`z_N`-coordinates of the two members of each pair (`linkSource`, `linkTarget`), the link is the
graph of an isometry `Υ_γ` (`linkIsometry`) of the positive space. The quantity `termDisc γ`
vanishes if and only if the spans of the frame and of its image under `γ` share a nonzero vector.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.link_inv_mul_mul_of_mem_besselU`,
  `New.Filling.frameDisc_frameGram_inv_mul_mul_of_mem_besselU`: the link and `New.frameDisc` are
  unchanged under `γ ↦ u⁻¹ γ u'` with `u`, `u'` in `besselU`.
* `New.NormOnePairOccursFrom.besselU_mul`, `New.NormOnePairOccursFrom.inv`: the norm-one pair
  condition is preserved by left multiplication by `besselU` and by inversion. With the invariance
  of the minors and of `termDisc`, this makes the cells stable (`New.Filling.isStable_hasCellRank`).
* `New.Filling.frameDisc_weylElem_mul`, `New.Filling.link_weylElem_mul_eq_iff`: values on the big
  cell, at `weylElem 𝔰.ϱ p * σ` with `σ` an isometry of the middle space. There the link determines
  `σ`.
* `New.Filling.linkIsometry`, `New.Filling.mem_link_iff_linkIsometry`: the isometry `Υ_γ`, and the
  link as its graph.
* `New.Filling.linkIsometry_frameImage_mulVec`, `New.Filling.mul_dotProduct_comp_indexX₀_eq_sub`:
  the link on combinations of the second frame, and the norm identity that follows.
* `New.Filling.termDisc_eq_zero_iff`: the criterion for the vanishing of `termDisc γ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.Form.splitGram`: the Gram matrix of `ϱ` hyperbolic planes and a middle space with Gram
  matrix `T`. The basis is `e₁, …, e_ϱ`, the middle vectors, `e*₁, …, e*_ϱ` (indices `New.eStar`).
* `New.Shape.Form.besselU`: the isometries that are block upper unitriangular for this basis.
* `New.Shape.Form.frameGram`: the `(ϱ + 1) × (ϱ + 1)` matrix of the products `h(f_j, γ f_l)` of the
  frame `f` with its image under `γ`, where `h` is the form `T.splitGram`.
* `New.Filling`: arithmetic data over a CM field `E`, among them the prime `S.N`. The matrix
  `S.ratMiddle E` is the Gram matrix of `X₀ ⊥ E z_N`, `S.ratGram` is its `splitGram`, `S.G E` is the
  group of isometries of `S.ratGram`, and `S.frameProducts γ` is the frame Gram matrix of `γ`.
* `New.frameDisc`: for a matrix of size `ϱ + 1` with leading minors `D_l`, the quantity
  `|D_{ϱ+1}|² - N² |D_ϱ|²`. Its value at `S.N` and the frame Gram matrix of `γ` is
  `New.Filling.termDisc γ`.
* `New.NormOnePairOccursFrom j γ`, the condition that a norm-one pair occurs from `j`: there is a
  `c` with `c c̄ = 1` such that, for every frame index `a ≥ j` (counted from `0`), the flags of `f`
  and `γ f` share a vector with leading coefficients `c` and `1` at `a`.

modules.title: Eichler-type unipotent elements, colouring bounds and reduced points
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
This file gives explicit elements of the congruence subgroup `New.Filling.classUnipotent` of
`New.Shape.Form.besselU` by Eichler's formula along isotropic basis vectors `e_a`. It also proves
counting tools for the remaining terms: weighted sums are bounded by colouring, and the index of a
scaled lattice is computed.
Finally, every point at the infinite places is moved to a reduced point by exactly one coset of
unipotent elements, so that the indicator of the reduced points is a partition of unity in boxes.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.exists_mem_classUnipotent_eq_one_add_smul`: the general element, along several `e_a`
  at once.
* `New.Filling.exists_eichler_classUnipotent`: an element with one prescribed row.
* `New.Filling.tsum_le_of_encard_range_le`: a weighted sum is at most the number of colours times
  the bound for one colour; `New.Filling.tsum_le_relIndex_pow_mul`: colours are residue classes
  modulo a subgroup of finite index.
* `New.Filling.IsResidueDomain.exists_mul_mem_reducedPoints_iff_rightCoset`: exactly one coset of
  unipotent elements moves a point to a reduced point (`New.Filling.reducedPoints`).
* `New.Filling.IsResidueDomain.isBoxPartitionOfUnity`: the indicator of the reduced points has the
  properties `New.Filling.IsBoxPartitionOfUnity`.

modules.title: The Bessel kernel and the integral of a class cutoff over the real unipotent group
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
This file proves that the kernel `New.Filling.besselKernel`, the tensor
`besselFn(y) ⊗ besselFn(γ⁻¹ y)^*` of Bessel functions at the infinite places, is continuous.
It bounds the amplitude `New.Filling.amplitude` by the integral of the norms
`New.Filling.amplitudeMajorant`. It then computes the integral of a class cutoff
`S.classCutoff c` over the real unipotent group as `S.unipotentCovolume`. The group is unfolded
one coordinate at a time (`New.Filling.rowCoords`). The integral is then a product of covolumes of
explicit lattices.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.enorm_amplitude_le`: the norm of the amplitude
  `∫ β_c(y) β_c'(γ⁻¹ y) W(y) ⊗ W(γ⁻¹ y)^* dy` is at most the integral of the norm of its integrand.
* `New.Filling.lintegral_classCutoff_eq_unipotentCovolume`: let `E` contain a primitive 5040th
  root of unity and let `S` be admissible. For every class `c` and archimedean point `y`, the
  integral of the cutoff `u ↦ S.classCutoff c (u y)` over the real unipotent group 𝖴_∞, for the
  product of the Haar measures `New.Shape.besselHaar`, is the number `S.unipotentCovolume`.

modules.title: Sums of amplitudes over blocks
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments

modules.title: Residue lifts, lattice charts and common flag vectors: which filling terms contribute
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
This file sorts the terms of the second moment of the filling theorem and shows which of them
contribute. Common vectors of two flags are moved up the flags by elementary linear algebra.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.mem_congruenceGL_iff_isIntMatrix_scaleAt`: for an integral idele `p` that is a unit
  at one of each pair of conjugate places, a unitary `k` is integral with row `o` congruent to that
  of `1` modulo `p` iff `k - 1` stays integral after dividing row `o` by `p` and column `o` by `p̄`.
* `New.Filling.inclHFin_mem_latticeStabilizer_iff`: `S.inclHFin k` is integral iff `k` is integral
  and its row `k₀` is congruent to that of `1` modulo `S.piN`.
* `New.Filling.MeetsAt`, `New.Filling.fixer`, `New.Filling.IsOpenElement`,
  `New.Filling.InScalarCoset`: the meeting places, and the subsets of the finite group.
* `New.Filling.amplitudeSum_eq_zero_of_not_charsAgree`: a stable set of terms none of which agrees
  contributes `0`.
* `New.Filling.mul_star_eq_and_pairOccursAt_of_le`,
  `New.Filling.exists_pairOccursInColumnsAt_top_of_meetsAt`: when the characters agree, the leading
  coefficients of a common vector of two flags have equal norms and recur at all higher indices over
  `E`; modulo a place above `M` where the flags meet, some pair not both zero occurs at the top
  index.
* `New.Filling.CharsAgree.exists_hasCellRank`: a term with agreeing characters and discriminant `0`
  has a cell rank.

Notions from other files:
* `S : New.Filling E 𝔰`: the filling data over the CM field `E`; `S.chosenPlaces i` is a set of
  places of `E` of norm the prime `S.levelPrime i` (`i = 0, 1`). The places above `M` are these and
  their conjugates, indexed by pairs `(w, false)` and `(w, true)`.
* `S.latticeStabilizer`, `S.reduction`, `S.ResidueGL`: the integral elements of the finite adelic
  unitary group, and their reduction to the product of the general linear groups over the residue
  fields `ResField w` at the chosen places.
* `New.frameImage γ`: the columns of `γ` at the indices of the frame `f = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`; so
  `frameImage 1` is the frame itself.
* `S.CharsAgree γ`, for rational `γ`: the character `S.unipotentChar` takes equal values on rational
  `u`, `u'` in `besselU` with `u γ = γ u'`. `S.Agrees s` is the analogue for `s` in `S.ResidueGL`.
* `besselH`, `besselU`, `besselS`: the unitary group of `X₀`, the unipotent group of the frame, and
  the Bessel subgroup that they generate.
* `Ô E`, `𝔸f E`: the integral finite adeles and the finite adeles of `E`.
modules.literature:
Take a rational element under which the unipotent character of the Poincaré series agrees with its
conjugate. For such an element, a vector shared by the standard frame and its image forces a
norm-one pair to occur. Take an integral adelic element k whose reduction modulo M agrees, and two
integral vectors orthogonal, in the standard form, to all vectors of f and kf but the last of each
(f is the frame). If the determinant δ of their products with these two last vectors is a finite
idele, the norm of the product of the primes over M where the span of f meets that of kf is at most
the index of δÔ in Ô (`New.Filling.meetNorm_le_genIndex_det`). This sorts the terms of the unfolded
second moment. Related work: Friedberg, Poincaré series for GL(n), 1987; Y. Liu, Relative trace
formulae toward Bessel and Fourier–Jacobi periods, 2014; Furusawa–Shalika, Central critical values
of degree four L-functions for GSp(4), Mem. AMS 782, 2003.

modules.title: The finite groups `Ū`, `H̄` and `R̄`
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
The factor of `Ū = S.reducedImage besselU` at each chosen place `w` consists of the block
unitriangular matrices over `𝔽_w` (`mem_reducedImage_besselU`). Counting free entries gives the
order of `Ū` (`card_reducedImage_besselU`). Each element of `R̄ = S.reducedImage besselS` is a
product of elements of `Ū` and `H̄ = S.reducedImage besselH` (`mem_reducedImage_besselS`), and
these two meet in the identity, giving `|R̄| = |H̄| |Ū|` (`card_reducedImage_besselS`). The order of
`H̄` is the index of `S.principalLevel.comap S.inclHFin` in `S.latticeStabilizer.comap S.inclHFin`
(`relIndex_comap_principalLevel`).

Notions from other files:
* `unitriangular lev R`: the invertible matrices over `R` that agree with `1` at the entries
  `(i, j)` with `lev j ≤ lev i`; `BesselIndex.level` is the level function of the Bessel basis.
* `S : Filling E 𝔰`: the data of the filling theorem, among them the sets `S.chosenPlaces i`.
* `S.latticeStabilizer`: the elements of the finite adelic unitary group `S.GFin` that are
  invertible over the integral adeles `Ô E`; `S.reduction` reduces them modulo the chosen places.

modules.title: The structure of a term
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
An element `γ` gives two frames, with the spans `A⁺` and `γ A⁺`, and two isotropic spaces `A` and
`γ A` with the intersection `I_γ`. This file describes `A⁺_γ = A⁺ + γ A⁺`, its radical and its
orthogonal complement, which modulo `I_γ` is isometric to `X₀^γ = X₀ ∩ Υ_γ⁻¹ X₀` by the map
`framePerpToX₀`. For an element that agrees and has `gr(γ) = 0` it proves that `A = A_{≤j} ⊕ I_γ`
and `γ A = γ A_{≤j} ⊕ I_γ` for `j = n - 1 - rk I_γ`, and that `j` is the cell rank of `γ`. It also
shows that `I_{u γ u'} = u I_γ` for `u`, `u'` in the unipotent group `U₀`, and that agreement
depends only on the double coset `U₀ γ U₀`. Finally it defines the set `Γ*` (`remainingTerms`) of
the terms that are left for the estimate of the second moment.

Here `n = ϱ + 1`, the frame is `e_1, …, e_{n-1}, z_N` (indexed from `0` in the code), `A` is spanned
by `e_1, …, e_{n-1}`, `A⁺ = A + E z_N`, and `A_{≤j}` is spanned by the first `j` vectors of the
frame. The space has rank `r` and `A^⊥ / A = X₀ ⊥ E z_N` with `X₀` of rank `k`. For `y` orthogonal
to `A` and `γ A` the classes of `y` and `γ⁻¹ y` are `y₀ + λ' z_N` and `y₀' + λ z_N`. A pair
`(μ, μ')` occurs at an index `a` if the two frames share a vector with coefficients `μ`, `μ'` at `a`
and `0` above `a`. In names, `_one` and `_coe` after a word for a span, as in `isotropicSpan_one`
and `flagSpan_coe`, refer to the frames `e_•` and `γ e_•`. The hypothesis `HasPrimitiveRoot5040 E`
says that `E` contains a primitive root of unity of order `5040`.

Notions from other files:
* `linkIsometry γ` is the link isometry `Υ_γ` of `X₀ ⊥ E z⁺` with `y₀ + λ z⁺ ↦ y₀' + λ' z⁺`.
* `termDisc γ` is `gr(γ) = |δ_n|² - N² |δ_{n-1}|²` for the leading minors `δ_j` of the matrix
  `frameProducts γ` of products of the two frames.
* `CharsAgree γ` (`γ` agrees) says that the character `unipotentChar` takes the same value at
  rational `u`, `u'` in `U₀` whenever `u γ = γ u'`.
* `HasCellRank j γ` says that one pair `(ζ, 1)` with `ζ ζ̄ = 1` occurs at all indices `a ≥ j`
  (`NormOnePairOccursFrom j γ`), that `δ_j ≠ 0`, and that `j = n` exactly when `gr(γ) ≠ 0`.

modules.title: The expansion of the squares and the second moment near the Bessel subgroup
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
This file proves the expansion of the squares and the bound on the second moment near `R̄₀`, where
`R̄₀ = reducedImage besselS` is the reduction of the Bessel subgroup. These results concern the
operators `P_s = P* s P`, stated in terms of their blocks. The terms in the Bessel subgroup give the
operator `r_ψ(s)`, which is `New.Filling.besselTranslate`, and the terms off it give `P_s - r_ψ(s)`.
Along the way it treats the terms of cell rank `0` and the cosets `ζ R̄₀` by integral `ζ ∈ E` with
`ζ ζ̄ = 1`, called roots of unity (these are the roots of unity of `E`, by Kronecker's theorem), and
it computes the blocks of the Bessel subgroup.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.sqrt_secondMoment_compl_besselS_le`: the expansion of the squares.
* `New.Filling.secondMoment_compl_besselS_le`: `P_s` is close to `r_ψ(s)` near `R̄₀`.

Notions from other files:
* `termsOver c s c'`: the rational `γ` such that `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'` (`translateByClassReps`) is integral
  with reduction `s`; such a `γ` lies over the block `(c, s, c')`.
* `amplitudeSum side T c s c'`: the sum of the amplitudes of the elements of `T` over that block.
* `secondMoment A Ω`: the sum of `‖A c s c'‖² / unipotentCovolume²` over all classes `c`, `c'` and
  `s ∈ Ω`.
* `reducedImage A`: the image in the finite group `ResidueGL` of the integral elements of `A`.

modules.title: The second moment over the whole group
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
This file proves the bound on the sum of the second moments of the operators `P_s = P* s P` over the
whole group, stated in terms of their blocks. It bounds the contribution of the cosets of `R̄₀` and
that of the elements that are not open.

The blocks of `P_s` are the complex conjugates of the sums `amplitudeSum` over all terms, divided by
`unipotentCovolume`, so `‖P_s‖²` (Hilbert–Schmidt norm) is the `secondMoment` of these sums at `s`.
In the same way the terms in the Bessel subgroup `R₀ = besselS` give `r_ψ(s)`, and those off it give
`P_s - r_ψ(s)`. The operator `r_ψ(s)` is `New.Filling.besselTranslate`; the passage from operators
to blocks is `New.Filling.HasAmplitudeBlocks`.

We write `R̄₀` for `reducedImage besselS`, `D_X` for `sourceDim`, `𝒟_id` for `identitySecondMoment`,
`𝒟_main` for `mainSecondMoment`, `b` for the parameter `S.b` of the filling, `p_i` for
`levelPrime i`, `M = p₀ p₁` for the level, `f` for the number of infinite places, `k = |κ|`,
`n = ϱ + 1` for the length of the frame, `e₁` for its vector of index `0` and `δ_l` for the leading
minors of `frameGram`. In `InScalarCoset ζ s` the scalar `ζ` is an integral adele, acting through
its residues.

* `New.Filling.sum_secondMoment_le`: `∑ ‖P_s‖² ≤ (1 + 9 b⁻⁴) 𝒟_main`, if `s ↦ ‖P_s‖²` has positive
  type and `‖P_1‖² ≤ 2 D_X`.
* `New.Filling.secondMoment_univ_eq_secondMoment_compl_besselS`: if `Ω` is disjoint from the
  reduction `R̄₀` of the Bessel subgroup, then the terms in the Bessel subgroup give `0` over `Ω`,
  so all terms and the terms off the Bessel subgroup have the same second moment over `Ω`.

Notions from other files:
* `termsOver c s c'`: the rational `γ` such that `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'` (`translateByClassReps`) is integral

* `amplitudeSum side T c s c'`: the sum of the amplitudes of the elements of `T` over that block.
* `secondMoment A Ω`: the sum of `‖A c s c'‖² / unipotentCovolume²` over all classes `c`, `c'` and

* `reducedImage A`: the image in the finite group `ResidueGL` of the integral elements of `A`.

modules.title: The second moments of the operators `P* s P`, and good forms
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
Let `S` be admissible filling data, with size parameter `b = S.b`. The finite group
`Ḡ = S.ResidueGL` has one factor for each of the two level primes `p_i = S.levelPrime i`, and
`R̄₀ = S.reducedImage besselS` is the image of the Bessel subgroup in it. The source is the space of
dimension `D_X = S.sourceDim` with coordinates indexed by the classes and the coordinates of the
Bessel function. For a map `P` from the source to a representation `ρ` of `Ḡ` put `P_s = P* ρ(s) P`;
all norms of operators are Hilbert–Schmidt norms. The file proves the two moment bounds for the
`P_s`, and deduces that `e₀ P` is almost an isometry for the projection `e₀` onto the target forms.
We write `𝒟_id = S.identitySecondMoment` and `𝒟_main = S.mainSecondMoment`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.HasAmplitudeBlocks`: the blocks of `P_s` are the conjugates of the amplitude sums,
  divided by the covolume.
* `New.Filling.besselTranslate`: the unitary representation `r_ψ` of `R̄₀` on the source, extended
  by `0`.
* `New.Filling.HasAmplitudeBlocks.sum_hilbertSchmidtNorm_sub_besselTranslate_sq_le`: over `R̄₀`
  times one factor of `Ḡ`, `∑ ‖P_s - r_ψ(s)‖² ≤ b⁻¹² 𝒟_id`.
* `New.Filling.HasAmplitudeBlocks.hilbertSchmidtNorm_sub_one_sq_le`: `‖P* P - 1‖² ≤ b⁻¹² D_X`.
* `New.Filling.HasAmplitudeBlocks.sum_hilbertSchmidtNorm_sq_le`: `∑ ‖P_s‖² ≤ (1 + 9 b⁻⁴) 𝒟_main`
  over `Ḡ`.
* `New.Filling.HasAmplitudeBlocks.isNearIsometry_piTensorElem_comp`: `e₀ P` is almost an isometry in
  mean square, with the error `5 b⁻⁴`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.reduction`: the homomorphism from the stabilizer `K = S.latticeStabilizer` of the
  lattice to `Ḡ` that reduces matrix entries modulo the chosen places above `p₀` and `p₁`.
* `New.Filling.termsOver`: the terms over a block `(c, s, c')`, the rational `γ` such that
  `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'` lies in `K` and has reduction `s`.
* `New.Filling.amplitudeSum`: the sum of the amplitudes of the terms of a set over a block.
* `New.Filling.identitySecondMoment`, `New.Filling.mainSecondMoment`: the numbers `#R̄₀ · D_X` and
  `D_X² / (deg · mass)`, with `deg = S.besselDegree` and the mass `New.mass` of the genus of the
  standard lattice of rank `r`.
