For the normalised Poincaré map `P`, the mean over level translates `s` of `‖P* s P‖²` is at most
nearly `D_X² / D₀`, with `D₀` the expected dimension of the target, and bad types carry little of
`P`. In rank one, Poisson summation on a product of two Kloosterman sides with a sharp diagonal term
is known in the literature. Related work: Herman, Beyond endoscopy for the Rankin–Selberg
L-function, 2011; Iwaniec–Li, The orthogonality of Hecke eigenvalues, 2007;
Michel–Ramakrishnan–Yang, Bessel periods on U(2,1)×U(1,1), 2023.

See `New.Spanning.SecondMoment.SpanningTheorem` and `New.Spanning.RemainingTerms.Sum` for related
work.

modules.title: Poincaré series of fitting spaces, unfolding, Petersson products and source form coordinates
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
This file builds Poincaré series from the Bessel functions of filling data S (`New.Filling`) on a
hermitian space V that fits S, and computes their Petersson products.

K = `New.Filling.latticeStabilizer` and K(M) = `New.Filling.principalLevel` are levels in the
lattice basis of S. Here K(M) is the kernel of reduction at the chosen places, and M in this
notation is the product of the two level primes, not an adelic point. For a graded space Y on V that
fits S, the groups attached to Y correspond to those of S under `New.Filling.Fits.adelicEquiv` and
`New.Filling.Fits.finiteEquiv`, and algebraic forms of level `S.sourceLevel` get coordinates indexed
by classes and indices.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.Fits`: V matches S; this gives the identifications `New.Filling.Fits.ratEquiv`
  (rational points), `New.Filling.Fits.realHomeomorph` (infinite places) and
  `New.Filling.Fits.finiteEquiv` (finite places).
* `New.Filling.Fits.cutBessel`, `New.Filling.Fits.poincareSeries`: a coordinate i of the Bessel
  function, cut off and supported on the coset of a class c, and the series ∑_a φ_a ∑_γ of these,
  a = (c, i).
* `New.Filling.Fits.petersson_poincare`: the Petersson products of translated series are the
  amplitude sums `New.Filling.amplitudeSum` times the volume of the level.
* `New.Filling.Fits.poincareMap`, `New.Filling.Fits.coe_poincareMap`: the series are forms of level
  `New.Filling.stdPrincipalLevel`, linear in φ.
* `New.Filling.Fits.sourceFormCoords`: algebraic forms of level `S.sourceLevel` as vectors of the
  Euclidean space on classes times indices.
* `New.Filling.Fits.finrank_levelSpace_eq_sourceDim`: the dimension of the space of these forms is
  the number of classes times the dimension of the weight, and it is positive.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.besselFn`: W_i(y), the product over the infinite places v of the i_v-th coordinate of
  the local Bessel function W_v at y_v. Only the full (not the cut) function is used: `.full`.
* `New.Filling.classRep`, `New.Filling.classUnipotent`, `New.Filling.classCutoff`: for a class c,
  its representative h_c, the group 𝖴_c(M) of rational unipotent u with h_c⁻¹ u h_c ∈ K(M), and a
  cutoff β_c at the infinite places whose translates under 𝖴_c(M) sum to 1.
* `New.Filling.termsOver`: the rational γ such that h_c⁻¹ γ h_c' lies in K and has reduction s.
* `New.Shape.Form.besselU`: the Bessel unipotent group 𝖴: the isometries of
  `New.Shape.Form.splitGram` T that are block upper unitriangular for the levels
  `New.BesselIndex.level`, so trivial on the middle block.
* X₀ is the hermitian space on κ with the standard form, all signs +1; U(X₀) is its unitary group.
modules.literature:
The file also contains known results stated on this proof's data: Poincaré series along a Bessel
subgroup and their unfolding. See `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Bruhat.FloorGroups`.

modules.title: The Bessel function as an integral over `R(F_∞)`
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
The group `R(F_∞)` is the product of the groups `R` at the infinite places. So the tensor product of
the local Bessel functions, each an integral over `R`, is one integral over `R(F_∞)`.

Notions from other files:
* `GInf E ε` is `G(F_∞)`, one copy of `U(diag ε)` for each infinite place of `E`, and `New.G E ε` is
  the adelic group `G(F_∞) × G(𝔸_f)` of the hermitian space `V`. The group `𝔰.G₁` is the complex
  unitary group of `ϱ` hyperbolic planes, the positive form with basis `𝔰.κ` and a negative vector.
* `S.Fits V l kw Y η`: the grading `Y` of `V` is standardly indexed, the Bessel system of the
  filling data `S` at each infinite place `v` has type `(l v, kw v)`, the kernel `typeKernel l ε` is
  idempotent, and the finite part of `V.x` is described by `S` and the central element `η`.
* `Y.besselGroup` is `R = U ⋊ H`, with `U = Y.unipotent` and `H` the unitary group of `κ`, embedded
  by `Y.inclX`; `Y.leviPart (n * Y.inclX a) = a`, and `Y.besselReal` is the group `R(F_∞)` of the
  real points of `R`.
* `𝔰.besselGraph` is the local group `R`, as pairs `(g, a)` in `G₁ × U(κ)` with `g (embedH a)⁻¹` in
  the local unipotent group `besselU`.
* `S.adelicToInf` takes the components at the infinite places in rescaled bases, and
  `h.realHomeomorph` identifies `G(F_∞)` with the product of copies of `G₁`: at each place it
  changes the basis and multiplies on the left by a fixed element, made from the distinguished
  matrix `V.x` of `V`.
* `𝔰.besselGraphMeasure` is the Haar measure `du dh` on the local group `R`, and
  `(l v).dsCoeffInFrame` is the coefficient of the discrete series of parameter `l v` on `G₁`.
* `S.besselSystem v` is the Bessel system at `v`. Its functions take values in `ℂ^I`, with
  `I = (S.besselSystem v).Index` finite, and `U(κ)` acts on `ℂ^I` by the unitary matrices
  `(S.besselSystem v).rep`. An element of `S.BesselCoord` is a choice of one index in `I` at each
  `v`, so `S.BesselCoord → ℂ` is the tensor product of the spaces `ℂ^I`.
* `WeylIndex 𝔰.κ kw` indexes a basis of the Weyl module of weight `kw`, in which forms take values.
* `h.weylBesselEquiv` is a fixed linear identification of the values of forms with the dual of the
  values of the Bessel function, and `ψ_U` is the generic character of `Y.unipotent`.
modules.literature: Related work on Bessel periods and on second moments is listed in `New.Spanning.Unfolding.Moments`.

modules.title: Masses of spheres and of frames
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
For the data `D` and an infinite place `v`, the file defines the mass `sph_l` of the unit sphere of
`ℂ ^ l` and the product `fr_v = N ^ k sph_{k+1} ⋯ sph_r`. By the approximate formula for the ratio
of masses in consecutive ranks, the product of the `fr_v` over the infinite places is at most
`N ^ (k f) mass_k / mass_r` up to a factor close to one, where `f` is the number of infinite places
and `mass_l` is the mass `New.mass` in rank `l`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.unitSphereMass`, `New.Data.frameMass`: the numbers `sph_l` and `fr_v`.
* `New.Data.prod_frameMass_mul_le`: the upper bound for the product of the `fr_v`.
* `New.Data.prod_frameMass_mul_openCellConst_eq`: the product of the `fr_v` in terms of the
  constants `New.Filling.siegelConst` and `New.Shape.openCellConst`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data`: the data: a CM field `E` with `f` infinite places (the type `D.Φ`) and root
  discriminant `rd = D.rootDisc`, a generator `P.deltaE D.towerExp` of its different, a prime level
  `N`, a weight `b`, the length `x` of the prime sum, and ranks `r = k + 2 ϱ + 1`.
* `New.Data.shape`: the shape of the hermitian space `Y₀` of rank `r`, which is the sum of `ϱ`
  hyperbolic planes, a space `X₀` of rank `k` and a line.
* `New.mass E l`: the mass of the genus of the standard hermitian lattice `O_E ^ l`.
* `New.Filling.siegelConst`: `c_S = (π ^ k / ((k - 1)! N ^ k)) ^ f |disc E| ^ (1/4) vol(Ô) ^ k`.
* `New.Shape.openCellConst`: `c_G = vol U(k) (2 π ^ k / (k - 1)!) / vol U(r)`.
* `New.volÔ E`: the volume `vol(Ô) = (2 / rd) ^ f` of the integral finite adeles.

modules.title: Filling data for admissible data: fit to Y₀, Bessel bounds, standing hypotheses
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
For admissible data `D`, the file shows that the filling data `New.Data.filling` fit the space `Y₀`.
It also shows that they satisfy the standing hypotheses `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`, so that the
general filling theorem applies.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.filling_fits`: the filling data `New.Data.filling` fit the space `Y₀`
  (`New.Filling.Fits`).
* `New.Data.sourceFormCoords`: source forms in coordinates, indexed by pairs (class, Bessel
  coordinate).
* `New.Data.goodProjTranslate`: the map from forms of level `M` on `Y₀` to the image of the good
  idempotent `New.Data.e₀`. It is a translation followed by this idempotent, scaled by the order of
  the finite group `𝖦`.
* `New.Data.card_besselSystem_le_pow`, `New.Data.card_besselCoord_le_pow`: the Bessel system at one
  place has at most `b ^ (2 k)` coordinates, and their tensor product at most `b ^ (2 k f)`.
* `New.Data.log_filling_besselDegree_mem_Icc`: two-sided bounds for the logarithm of the degree of
  the Bessel systems.
* `New.Data.card_mul_card_classes_mul_prod_le`, `New.Data.card_sq_mul_mass_mul_prod_le`: two
  products built from group orders, class number, masses, dimensions and degrees are at most
  `(1 + b⁻⁹)` times `New.Filling.mainSecondMoment`. `New.Data.card_mul_prod_frameMass_le` states
  both.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.spaceY`: for an index `j`, the hermitian space `Y_j` with its adelic frame, hence its
  lattice `𝖬_j`, chosen as in `New.Data.exists_space_isStd_of_le_and_gram_eq_of_lt`. Only `j = 0`
  occurs in this file.
* `New.Data.chosenGL`: The finite group 𝖦 = ∏ GL_r(𝔽_w), over the chosen places w above p₀ and p₁.
* `New.Data.targetParameter`: The entry i (from 0) of the target parameter at v: k/2 − 1 − i for
  i < k − 1, and Δ/2 − w_{i+2−k}(v) otherwise, where Δ/2 = `D.halfGap` and
  w_j(v) = `D.liftWeight j v`.
* `New.Filling.besselDegree`: The product over infinite places of the degrees of the Bessel systems.
* `New.Data.logLevelTarget`: a number `λ`, built from the mean of the `log (D.weight v)`, from
  `log (M rootDisc / 2π)` and from `log b`, with `λ ≤ log N ≤ λ + √(log b)`.

modules.title: The Poincaré map as a Poincaré series of the Bessel function
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
There are a real point `g₀` and a linear form `t` for which the form `D.poincareAt g₀ t φ`, which
represents the Bessel period of `φ`, is the Poincaré series of the Bessel function; the map
`D.poincare` is defined by such a choice. Pair the series with a form `y` of the conjugate type.
Unfolding gives a sum over the classes `c` of integrals over `U_c \ G(F_∞)`. Insert the integral
formula of the Bessel function, an integral over `R(F_∞)`, and move the quotient by `U_c` to that
variable; the conjugate kernel reproduces `y`, and the sum
`∑_c ∫_{U_c \ R(F_∞)} 𝒲 (s, h_c) y (s g₀, h_c) ds` remains. The period is a multiple of the same
sum, because `[R] / J'` is the disjoint union of the `U_c \ R(F_∞)`.

Notions from other files:
* `S.Fits V l kw Y η`: the space `V` with the grading `Y` and the central element `η` fits the
  filling data `S`; it identifies the adelic group of `V` with that of `S`.
* `h.poincareSeries φ`: the series `g ↦ ∑_a φ_a ∑_{γ ∈ G(F)} h.cutBessel a (γ g)`, where `a` runs
  over the pairs `(c, i)` of a class and a coordinate, and `h.cutBessel (c, i)` is `β_c` times the
  `i`-th coordinate of the Bessel function on `G(F_∞) × h_c J` and zero elsewhere.
* `Y.besselGroup`, `Y.unipotent`, `Y.inclX`: the group `R(𝔸)`, its unipotent radical and the
  inclusion of `H(𝔸)`, the unitary group of the form on the part `𝔰.κ` of the basis;
  `Y.ratBessel` is `R(F)`, `Y.besselReal` is `R(F_∞)`, `Y.besselFin` is `R(𝔸_fin)`, and
  `Y.besselMeasure` computes integrals over `[R] = R(F) \ R(𝔸)`.
* `J = S.stdPrincipalLevel` is the principal level, and `J' = R(𝔸_fin) ∩ J`.
* `h_c = h.classPoint c`, `U_c = S.classUnipotent c`, `β_c = S.classCutoff c`: the image in
  `R(𝔸_fin)` of `c.out * η⁻¹`, with `c.out` the representative of the class `c`; the group of
  rational unipotents `u` with `h_c⁻¹ u h_c ∈ J`; and a weight at the infinite places whose
  translates under `U_c` add up to one. An integral over a quotient by `U_c` is written as an
  integral against `β_c`.
* `h.besselChar`: the character of `R(𝔸)` given by the entries at the simple roots. The hypothesis
  `hj_genericConst` is `ȷ Y.genericConst = -(M ϖ)⁻¹`, with `ȷ = WeilData.j`, `M = S.M`,
  `ϖ = S.deltaE` and `Y.genericConst` the constant of `ψ_U = Y.unipotentChar`; it makes
  `h.besselChar` equal to `ψ_U` on `U(𝔸)`.
* `Y.sourceFn t φ`: the function `𝒲 (u a) = ψ_U (u) t (ǎ_∞⁻¹ φ (a_fin))` on `R(𝔸)`, where `ǎ_∞`
  is the action `conjWeylRep` of the real component `a_∞` of `a`.
modules.literature: Unfolding a Poincaré series against an automorphic form is standard.

modules.title: Discriminants of sublattices, Siegel's lemma and a height zeta function of subspaces
modules.note:
Let `E` be a CM field containing a primitive 5040th root of unity, `𝔸f E` its finite adeles and
`Ô E` their integers. A lattice is given by an adelic basis: a matrix over `E`, embedded by
`New.Filling.finAdeleMatrix`, times a matrix over the finite adeles. Subspaces `T` of `E^κ` have
heights relative to the lattice `E^κ ∩ u Ô^κ` of a finite adelic unitary matrix `u : New.Gf E κ`.
Here `d T = New.Filling.sublatticeDiscriminant u.val.val_inv T` is the discriminant of `T ∩ u Ô^κ`;
the first argument proves `u u⁻¹ = 1`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.sublatticeBasis`, `New.Filling.sublatticeDiscriminant`: a basis and the discriminant
  of the points of a subspace `V` that `H` makes integral.
* `New.Filling.siegel_lemma`: a subspace of codimension `s` is cut out by `s` short vectors.
* `New.Filling.tsum_sublatticeDiscriminant_inv_le`: an explicit bound for `∑ (d T)⁻¹ ^ (#κ + 1)`
  over the subspaces `T` of `E^κ` of codimension `s`. It follows from `New.Filling.siegel_lemma`:
  each `T` is charged to its tuple of vectors, and a packing bound sums over the lattice.

Notions from other files:
* `New.CMType E`: `E` is a CM number field (it extends `NumberField E` and `IsCMField E`) with a
  chosen complex embedding `Φ v` inducing each infinite place `v`.
* `New.IsPrimitiveMatrix O X`: `X` has entries in `O` and a left inverse with entries in `O`.
* `New.genIndex a`: the inverse of the factor by which a unit `a` scales Haar measure, `0` for a
  non-unit.
modules.literature:
Known result: Siegel's lemma over number fields (Bombieri–Vaaler). It is stated for lattices in the
genus of the standard hermitian lattice over a stably unramified CM field
(`New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040`: `E` contains a primitive `5040`-th root of unity). A subspace is cut
out by lattice vectors; a power of the product of their norms is bounded by an explicit constant,
depending on the degree, the codimension and the root discriminant, times its discriminant. Source:
E. Bombieri, J. Vaaler, On Siegel's lemma, Invent. Math. 73 (1983).

modules.title: The box
modules.note:
Let `S : Filling E 𝔰` be admissible data for a CM field `E` and a shape `𝔰`, with `M = S.M` the
level and `b = S.b`. Consider the tuples of complex numbers, one for each infinite place, modulo
`M 𝓞_E`, and fix a measurable set `D` of representatives, each coordinate of each point of `D`
having modulus at most `b ^ 26`.

An archimedean point `y` is reduced if the entries above the diagonal of its triangular matrix
`S.ratTriangle y` lie in `D`. It is boxed if it is reduced and lies in the cut at every place `v`,
that is, `besselLength (y v) ≤ b ^ (6 n + 2)`, where `n = 𝔰.n = 𝔰.ϱ + 1`.

Notions from other files:
* `frameVector z a`: for `z` in `𝔰.G₁`, the image of the `a`-th frame vector under `z⁻¹`;
  `orthoFrame z` is the result of the Gram–Schmidt process on these vectors.
* `gramSchmidtMatrix z`: the unitriangular matrix of the coefficients of `frameVector z` in
  `orthoFrame z`; `S.ratTriangle` reads it in the rational frame.
* `besselLength z`: the infimum of `‖s * z‖ + 1` over `s` in the Bessel subgroup.
* `frameBox r`: the points at which all frame vectors have length at most `r`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.exists_isResidueDomain`: such a set `D` exists.
* `New.Filling.boxedPoints`: the boxed points.
* `New.Filling.mul_mem_boxedPoints_iff`: invariance under the unipotent elements fixing the frame.
* `New.Filling.mem_frameBox_of_mem_boxedPoints`: at a boxed point the frame vectors have length at
  most `b ^ (37 n)`.

modules.title: Links, lifts and gauges of a term
modules.note:
The data are `S : New.Filling`, and terms are rational elements `γ` of the unitary group
`New.Filling.G`. The frame is `f = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`, `A` is the span of the `e_a` and `X₀` that of
the `x_i`. `S.frameProducts γ` is the matrix of products of `f` with `γ f`, and `S.HasCellRank j γ`
says that `γ` has cell rank `j`. `New.Filling.minorNorm j γ` is the absolute norm of the leading
`j × j` minor of `S.frameProducts γ`, scaled by a power of `N` when `j = ϱ + 1`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.gram_linkForm_eq_zero_of_le_link`: the link is isotropic for `S.linkForm`.
* `New.Filling.linkMetric` is a totally positive form (`New.Filling.linkMetric_posDef`), and
  `New.Filling.linkDiscSq` is the squared discriminant of a lattice for it.
* `New.Filling.HasIntegralLifts`: the predicate that the columns of an adelic matrix are images
  under `New.linkMatrix γ` of vectors of `h_c Λ₀` that are adelic combinations of rational vectors
  orthogonal to `A` and `γ A`.
* `New.Filling.paddedLeading`: the first `j` rows of a matrix, completed by rows of `1`; its
  determinant is the leading minor of order `j` (`New.Filling.det_paddedLeading`). For the matrix
  `S.frameProducts γ` its inverse gives the vectors that `f` and `γ f` share
  (`New.Filling.HasCellRank.exists_shared_frame_vector`).
* `New.Filling.latticeDisc`, `New.Filling.isotropicRowsIndex`, `New.Filling.torsionIndex`: a
  discriminant and two lattice indices. `New.submoduleIndex M M'` is the index of `M ⊓ M'` in `M'`,
  `New.colLattice` a column span.
* `New.Filling.subframeMinor`: the minor `δ_*(γ)`, nonzero for a term with a cell rank
  (`New.Filling.HasCellRank.subframeMinor_ne_zero`).
* `New.Filling.minorGauge`, `New.Filling.maxGauge`: the gauges of a term.
  `New.Filling.IsNearRepresentative` marks the kept terms, and `New.Filling.IsNearTermAt` selects
  the terms that are counted.

Notions from other files:
* `New.link`: the pairs of middle coordinates of `t` and `γ⁻¹ t`, for `t` orthogonal to `A` and
  `γ A`; `New.linkMatrix γ` is the matrix of the map that sends `t` to this pair.
* `New.framePair γ`: the matrix `(f | γ f)` of the two frames; `New.isotropicFramePair γ` is its
  part `(A | γ A)`.
* `New.Filling.Classes`: the classes `c` of a finite double coset space of `U(X₀)`; `h_c` is the
  representative of `c`, and `S.translateByClassReps c c' γ` is `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'`.
* `New.Filling.classCoord`: `S.classCoord c` takes rational coordinates to coordinates in the
  basis of `h_c Λ₀`, in which the middle Gram matrix is `S.latticeMiddle`; in rational coordinates

* `New.genIndex`: the generalised index `[a]` of an adele `a`; it is `0` for a non-unit.

modules.title: Frames of near terms: short shared vectors and moves between frames
modules.note:
This file proves lemmas for counting the frames `γ f` of the remaining terms `p = (c', γ)` modulo
moves. Here `f = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)` is the standard frame, `New.frameImage γ` is the frame `γ f`, and
`Z = S.frameProducts γ` is the matrix of products of `f` with `γ f`. At boxed points the frames are
uniformly independent, so the vectors shared by the two frames of a near term are short.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.IsNearTermAt.eq_of_frameImage_eq`: near terms moved by elements of
  `New.Filling.classUnipotent₀` are determined by their frames.
* `New.Filling.HasCellRank.mulVec_eStar_eq_zero_and_sum_indexX₀_le`,
  `New.Filling.col_eq_zero_of_norm_lt_one`: certain vectors have a short `X₀`-part, and a short
  vector of the lattice of `c` in `X₀` is zero.
* `New.Filling.exists_mem_classUnipotent₀_frameImage_mul_eq`: take two terms with the same integral
  `S.frameProducts`, with nonzero leading minor of order `j`, and the same shared vectors, whose
  frames agree outside the first block of rows and differ in that block by `S.frameModulus` times an
  integral matrix. Then an element of `S.classUnipotent₀ c` carries one frame to the other.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.paddedLeading`: the first j rows of Z, completed by rows of the identity matrix.
* `New.Filling.HasCellRank`: γ has cell rank j, that is, the flags of the two frames share vectors
  from the index j on (`NormOnePairOccursFrom`), the leading minor D_j of Z(γ) is nonzero, and the
  discriminant `termDisc` of γ is nonzero exactly when j = ϱ + 1.
* `New.Filling.classUnipotent₀`: the rational unipotent elements of level M for the class c that fix
  every vector of the frame.
* `New.Filling.IsNear`: γ is near if y and γ⁻¹y are both boxed points for some archimedean y.

modules.title: The covolume of the lattice of columns
modules.note:
The tuples of vectors of the lattice `Λ ∩ X₀` of a class form a lattice in the product of the
complex places. The real inner product of two of its points is an integer, so its covolume is at
least `1`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.columnLattice`, `New.Filling.exists_isAddFundamentalDomain_columnLattice`: the
  lattice of tuples of vectors of `Λ ∩ X₀` and its fundamental domain.

Notions from other files:

* `S : Filling E 𝔰`: the data of the filling theorem over the CM field `E` for the shape `𝔰`; the
  space `X₀` has a basis indexed by `𝔰.κ`, a set of `𝔰.k` elements.
* `c : S.Classes`: a class of the definite unitary group of `X₀`, with lattice `Λ`.
* `S.classCoordX₀ c`: the matrix that writes vectors of `X₀` in a basis of `Λ`; thus a vector lies
  in `Λ ∩ X₀` if its image under this matrix is integral.
* `Φ v`: the chosen complex embedding of `E` at the infinite place `v`.
* `Ô E`, `finAdeleMatrix q`: the integral finite adeles, and the matrix `q` over the finite adeles.

modules.title: The weight of Schur's test at one real place
modules.note:
`New.Shape.G₁` is the unitary group of the form `New.Shape.J₁`, which consists of `ϱ` hyperbolic
planes, a positive part `X₀` indexed by `κ` and one negative vector `z`. The frame is
`f = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`, `A` is the span of the `e_a`, and `V₋` is the `-1` eigenspace of `J₁`. The
weight is a power `ν(y) ^ (-(k + i))`, `k = dim X₀`, of the ratio of the volumes of the projections
of the frames `γ f` and `f` to the negative space `y V₋`. Let norm-one pairs occur for `γ` from

`v` lie in `X₀` and move affinely when `y` is moved by a unipotent element `g` that fixes the frame.
Since `ν` for `γ` at `g y` is `ν` for `g⁻¹ γ` at `y`, the point `y` stays fixed here and `γ` is
replaced by `g⁻¹ γ`.

modules.title: Discriminants of lattices and sums over sublattices
modules.note:
Lattices of rational subspaces of a space with the standard hermitian form, written over `Ô`;
their discriminants; and a bound for the sum of a negative power of the index over all sublattices
of finite index.

The bound for the sum over sublattices is a consequence of Hey's formula for the zeta function of a
lattice. Here it is proved directly, by induction on the rank, over any
commutative ring whose ideals of finite index are principal.

The formula that compares the discriminant of `L ∩ W` with that of the dual lattice in `W^⊥` is
`New.Filling.jacobi_perp_discriminant`, stated for Gram determinants.

modules.title: Near terms in the filling theorem: the bound for an orbit, the tail and the open-cell term
modules.note:
This file defines the size allotted to a near orbit of terms `γ` and bounds the tail and the
open-cell term by it. The data are `S : New.Filling E 𝔰` for a shape `𝔰`, with the size hypotheses
`New.Filling.IsAdmissible`, which compare all constants with powers of the large parameter `b`.
For admissible data, if `S.termDiscNorm γ` is at least 1, then the orbit bound at the top cell
rank, with that norm as gauge, bounds the open-cell term of `γ` and, if `γ` is near, also the tail.
Here `k = |κ|`, `f` is the number of infinite places and `τ = b^(kf/4)`.

* `New.Filling.cellRankSecondMoment`: the second moment D_j against which the size of a term of cell

  the identity second moment below it.
* `New.Filling.orbitBound`: the bound allotted to a near orbit, as a function of its cell rank j and
  of its gauge x. It is τ² (D_j / (n_p (M^(2j'f) x)^k))^(1/2) with j' = min ϱ j, in units of the
  covolume ν.

modules.title: Orthogonal lifts and the two isotropic lists of a link
modules.note:
Let `γ` have cell rank `j`, let `Λ` be the lattice of a class, `A` the span of `e₁, …, e_ϱ`,
`I = A ∩ γ A`, and let `z` be the last vector of the frame, of norm `-N`. This file defines
orthogonal lifts of a basis `v` of the link of `γ`. These are vectors orthogonal to `A` and `γ A`
over the columns of `(0 | v)`, whose first columns form a basis of `I`. It proves that such lifts

with `z` and `γ z`. It then adjoins two vectors `z'`, `z''` of norm `N` and computes the
discriminant of the isotropic lists `(e_a, z + z')` and `(γ e_a, γ z + z'')`, `a < j`. It also
shows that `torsionIndex k` divides the index of the classes of the `e_a` and `k e_a` in the
integral vectors of their span, for finite-adelic `k`.

modules.title: The cut: from the lattice of a link to the vectors common to two links
modules.note:
Let `A` be the span of `e₁, …, e_ϱ`, `Λ` the lattice of a class and `M` the level. The vectors of
`Λ` orthogonal to `A` and `γ A` whose part in `A` is divisible by `M` give a lattice `L⁺_γ` in the
link of a term `γ`. We descend from it to its intersection with the link of a second term `γ'`,
and from there to the part orthogonal to `z⁺` and `Υ_γ⁻¹ z⁺`, which lies in
`L_γ = S.termLattice c c' γ`. The last step costs at most a principal minor of their Gram matrix.
So the discriminant of this part, times the torsion index `S.torsionIndex`, the discriminant of
the projection to the complement of the intersection and a gain `x` from the places where the
residue meets, is at most the gauge `S.levelGauge` of the term (`nonempty_linkSplitting` below).

* `New.Filling.HasCellRank.abs_norm_minor_gram_linkVectors_mul_le`,
  `New.Filling.minorNorm_sq_le_linkDiscSq_mul`: the cost of the cut, in the three cases of rank
  `0`, `1` and `2`. The first bounds the principal minors of the Gram matrix of the two vectors;
  the second is the resulting lower bound for the discriminant of a lattice in the link on whose
  span the `z`-forms are injective.
* `New.Filling.LinkSplitting`, `New.Filling.nonempty_linkSplitting`: the splitting of a link along
  its intersection with a second link.
* `New.Filling.HasIntegralLifts.isIntMatrix_linkForm`: for two terms over one block, the form
  `S.linkForm / M` is integral on pairs of lifts.

modules.title: The gain: a discriminant bound for the common lattice of two terms over one block
modules.note:
Take two terms `γ`, `γ'` over one block `(c, s, c')` whose `s` agrees. The square of the
discriminant of their common lattice `L₁₂` is at most the product of their values of `S.levelGauge`,
divided by a power of `M / 2` if the links differ, and by the square of the norm of the places at
which `s` meets if the links are equal and `S.termDisc` does not vanish
(`New.Filling.pairDiscriminant_sq_le`). A block is a pair of classes `c`, `c'` with an element `s`
of the finite group `S.ResidueGL`. The element `s` agrees if the character `S.unipotentChar` takes
the same value on any two integral unipotents `u`, `u'` whose reductions satisfy `ū s = s ū'`.

The proof descends from the lattice `L⁺_γ` of each link in three steps.

* The congruence (`New.Filling.LinkSplitting.one_le_mul_linkDiscSq`): passing to the intersection of
  the two links gains a power of `M / 2`, as `γ γ'⁻¹` is `1` modulo `M` on `Λ`.
* The cut (`New.Filling.nonempty_linkSplitting`): passing to `commonLink γ γ'`, the vectors of `X₀`
  that both links send to one vector of `X₀`. This gives
  `New.Filling.torsionIndex_mul_discriminant_commonPart_le`, a bound for the parts `S.commonPart` of
  the lattices of the two terms, with the torsion indices saved.
* The index (`New.Filling.submoduleIndex_pairLattice_dvd_torsionIndex`): passing to `L₁₂` costs at
  most the torsion index of the other term.

Here `A` is the span of `e₁, …, e_ϱ`, `Λ` is the lattice of the class `c`, `M` is the level and
`L_γ = S.termLattice c c' γ`. The lattice `L⁺_γ` consists of the vectors of the link of `γ` with an
integral lift whose part in `A` is divisible by `M` (`New.Filling.HasLevelLifts`). The space `X₀`
and the line `E z` make up the middle space of the frame, and `X₀ ⊥ E z⁺` is positive definite, with
`z⁺` of norm `S.N`. The torsion index of `γ` is `S.torsionIndex (S.translateByClassReps c c' γ)`.

Notions from other files:
* `link γ`: the pairs of classes in `A^⊥ / A` of `t` and `γ⁻¹ t`, for `t` orthogonal to `A + γ A`.
* `linkIsometry γ`: the isometry `Υ_γ` of `X₀ ⊥ E z⁺` that the link of `γ` determines.
* `S.termsOver c s c'`: the rational `γ` with `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'` in the stabilizer of the lattice and
  reducing to `s`; this product is `S.translateByClassReps c c' γ`.
* `S.HasCellRank j γ`: `γ` has cell rank `j ≤ ϱ + 1`, the top one exactly if `S.termDisc γ ≠ 0`.
* `S.levelGauge j c c' γ`: the gauge `𝗀*` of the term, a positive real bound for discriminants.

modules.title: The sum over pairs of near terms
modules.note:
For a fixed class `c`, a pair of near terms over a block `(c, s, c')` is sorted by its label, a
component of `s` in the reduced image of the Bessel subgroup, and by its common lattice. Over a
given lattice and label there are few terms, and the sum over the lattices is bounded.

The main notions used in the statements:
* a class `c : S.Classes` is a double coset of the unitary group of the definite space `X₀` at the
  finite adeles, with representative `h_c`;
* a block is a triple `(c, s, c')`, with `s` in the finite group `S.ResidueGL`. A rational isometry
  `γ` is a term over it if `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'` is integral with reduction `s`;
* `S.IsNearPairOverAgreeingBlock c c' q`: the two terms in `q` are near, are the chosen
  representatives of their double cosets, have a cell rank, and lie over one block `(c, s, c')`
  whose `s` agrees (`S.Agrees s`);
* `commonLink γ γ'`: the subspace of `X₀` that two terms have in common; its dimension is the rank
  of their common lattice `L₁₂ = S.pairLattice c c' γ γ'`, which has corank `l` if this dimension is
  `k - l`;
* `S.termLattice c c' γ`: the lattice `L_γ ⊆ Λ ∩ X₀` of a term, where `Λ` is the adelic lattice of
  the class `c` and `Λ ∩ X₀` is `S.classLatticeX₀ c`.

The main result is `New.Filling.sum_pairDiscriminant_inv_le`.

modules.title: The remaining terms: a bound for their sum
modules.note:
Size, gain and count are combined: pairs of terms that do not lie in the same link class contribute
at most `b ^ (-k f) 𝒟_id`, and pairs in the same link class gain the norm of the places at which the
block meets.

* `New.Filling.sum_termSize_mul_le`: sets of near pairs, one for each two classes, with
  `τ ^ (l + 6) D η ^ (-k) ≤ B` contribute at most `τ B` in all. Here `l` is the corank of the common
  lattice, the gain `η` is such that `(d η)²` is at most the product of the two gauges for the
  discriminant `d` of that lattice, and `D` bounds the second moments of both cell ranks.
* `New.Filling.sum_termSize_mul_not_inSameLinkClass_le`: pairs with different links, or with equal
  links and `𝗀 = 0`, contribute at most `b ^ (-k f) 𝒟_id`.
* `New.Filling.sum_termSize_mul_inSameLinkClass_le`: pairs with equal links and `𝗀 ≠ 0` over blocks
  that meet at places of total norm at least `z` contribute at most `(b ^ (2 f) / z) ^ k 𝒟_main`.
* `New.Filling.secondMoment_remainingTerms_le`, `New.Filling.linkSecondMoment_le_of_le_meetNorm`:
  the resulting bounds for the second moment of the remaining terms.

Here `b = S.b` is the scale, `M = S.M` the congruence level, `k = 𝔰.k` and `n = 𝔰.n` are sizes of
the shape, `f` is the number of infinite places, `τ = S.tailScale = b ^ (k f / 4)` is the number
whose powers may be lost, `𝗀 = S.termDisc`, `𝒟_id = S.identitySecondMoment` and
`𝒟_main = S.mainSecondMoment`.

Notions from other files:
* `S.cellRank γ`: the cell rank of a rational element `γ`, the index of its cell.
* `S.termsOver c s c'`: the rational elements that are integral in the position given by the classes
  `c`, `c'` and have reduction `s`; the triple `(c, s, c')` is called a block.
* `S.IsNearPairOverAgreeingBlock c c' q`: both terms of `q` are near, are the chosen elements of
  their orbits, have a cell rank, and lie over one block `(c, s, c')` whose `s` agrees
  (`S.Agrees s`).
* `S.pairDiscriminant c c' γ γ'`: the discriminant of the common lattice `L₁₂` of two terms, a
  lattice in `commonLink γ γ'`; its corank is `k - finrank E (commonLink γ γ')`.
* `S.termSize c c' γ`: the bound `τ² (D_j / (n_p G ^ k)) ^ (1 / 2)` for the orbit of `γ`, with the
  second moment `D_j = S.cellRankSecondMoment j`, the gauge `G = S.levelGauge j c c' γ` and
  `n_p = S.pairCountScale`.
modules.literature:
The second moment of the Poincaré series expands over pairs of rational elements congruent mod `M`.
Discriminant gains, lattice counts and a weighted Schur test show that degenerate terms and pairs
with different links are negligible, and that the remaining terms shrink where frames meet mod `M`,
which isolates the main term. Discarding small cells and off-diagonal terms of Petersson-type and
relative trace formulas by congruences and counts is known in the literature. Related work:
Michel–Ramakrishnan–Yang, Bessel periods on U(2,1)×U(1,1), 2023; Kowalski–Saha–Tsimerman, Local
spectral equidistribution for Siegel modular forms, 2012; Blomer, Density theorems for GL(n), 2023.

modules.title: Sieve systems over places: products, positivity and lower semicontinuity
modules.note:
An abstract sieve. A system `New.SieveSystem` over a ring `C` with a measure (a place, or a product
of places) consists of forms `J i p q`, `i ≤ n + 1`, on pairs of sequences ("heads"), each but the
last the integral of the next one over a common entry, with bounds `B₀`, `Λ`, `β`.

* `New.SieveSystem.pi`: a product of finitely many systems on `ℂ` (one for each real
  place in the application) and one more system is a system.
* `New.SieveSystem.integrable_sum_update`, `New.SieveSystem.integral_sum_update`,
  `New.SieveSystem.norm_integral_mul_sum_update_le`: sum the forms `J (i + 1)` over all pairs of
  heads from one finite family, with a common entry at position `i ≤ n`. The sum is integrable in
  the common entry, its integral is the sum of the `J i`, and its twisted integrals are bounded by
  `β` and `Λ`. `New.SieveSystem.integrable_and_integral_sum_update` collects the three.
* `New.SieveSystem.sum_nonneg`, `New.SieveSystem.lowerSemicontinuousAt_sum`: such a sum is
  nonnegative, and its real part is lower semicontinuous in a parameter `x : C` at each point where
  every head is continuous. `New.SieveSystem.sum_nonneg_and_lowerSemicontinuousAt` collects the two.
* `New.dampedPower`, `New.headWeight`: the decay in the frequency and the weights `Λ` of the heads
  at the real places.

modules.title: The orbital integral at the finite places is a Kloosterman sum
modules.note:
Let `𝖴` be the unipotent group `New.Shape.Form.besselU` over a finite place, or a product of finite
places, let `K(M)` be the principal congruence subgroup of a level `M`, and let `ψ_𝖴` be the
character of `𝖴`. The finite Bessel function `χ` is `ψ_𝖴(u)` on `u K(M)` and zero off `𝖴 K(M)`.

* `New.Floors.PlaceData.kloostermanSum`: the sum of `ψ_𝖴(u) conj ψ_𝖴(u')` over the pairs `u`, `u'`
  in `𝖴 / (𝖴 ∩ K(M))` with `u⁻¹ x u' ∈ s K(M)`.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.besselOrbitalIntegral_besselVector_apply`: the entry
  `(a, b)` of the orbital integral of the finite Bessel vector at `x` is the volume of `K(M)` times
  the Kloosterman sum of `x` at `s = a b⁻¹`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.Form.splitGram`: the Gram matrix of `𝔰.ϱ` hyperbolic planes and a middle space with
  Gram matrix `T`. The group `T.G` is its unitary group.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData ι T (m + 1)`: the data of a place. They include the level `M = F.levelUnit`
  and a basis of the middle space made of `m + 2` hyperbolic pairs and orthonormal vectors indexed
  by `ι`.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData`: these data come from the lattice of vectors
  integral over `P.integers`, with conditions on the rank, the character of the place and the group.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.extendedBesselChar`: the finite Bessel function `χ`.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IntermediateGroup.besselVector`: for a group `Z` between `K(M)` and the
  integral points, the vector of the translates of `χ` by the cosets of `K(M)` in `Z`.
* `New.besselOrbitalIntegral μ W x`: the orbital integral of `W(y) ⊗ W(x⁻¹ y)^*` over `y`.

modules.title: Sums over frequencies
modules.note:
The frequencies are the elements `ν` of a totally complex number field `E`. If `E` has `f` infinite
places, the sum of `∏_v [ν]_v ^ (-3)` over any finite subset of `E` is at most `C ^ f` with
`C = 64 * 38 * e ^ 4`. At an infinite place `[ν]_v` is `(max 1 |ν|_v) ^ 2`, with `|ν|_v` the usual
absolute value, and the finite places together give the norm of the denominator of `ν`. The numbers
with a given denominator `𝔟` lie in `N 𝔟` cosets of the ring of integers, each coset is counted by
small squares, and the sum over `𝔟` is at most the value at `2` of the Dedekind zeta function.

Notions from other files:
* `Φ v`: the chosen complex embedding of `E` that induces the infinite place `v`
  (`PlaceEmbedding E`).

modules.title: One-sided Poisson summation, sums over frequencies, and the sieve over all places
modules.note:
The sieve over the infinite places of the CM field `E` and a finite set `T` of finite places, which
bounds the main term.

* `New.Filling.charOnPlaces`, `New.Filling.globalChar`: the character of the product of the
  completions at `T`, and its product with the characters at the infinite places.
* `New.Filling.sum_ratPoint_le_mul_add_integral_of_fourier_le`: one-sided Poisson summation over the
  infinite places and `T`, at rational points integral off `T`.
* `New.Filling.entryDensity`, `New.Filling.densitySum`: the sum of densities at a common next entry,
  and the sums of densities in which the first `i` entries are summed over `A`.
* `New.Filling.densitySum_succ_le_mul_densitySum_add`: each sum of densities is bounded by the one
  before plus an error, up to the constant of Poisson summation (`New.Filling.poissonConst`).
* `New.Filling.densitySum_le`: the bound after all entries are removed in turn.
* `New.Filling.sieve`: the sieve for the product of one system for each infinite place and one
  system at `T`, read at rational points (`New.Filling.ratPoint`).

Conventions: `𝔰.k` and `𝔰.n = 𝔰.ϱ + 1` are parameters of the shape `𝔰`; in
`New.Filling.frequency_term_le` and `New.Filling.sum_frequencies_le`, `k` is any natural number.
`Φ v` is the chosen embedding of `E` at the infinite place `v`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling`: the data `S`, among them the size parameter `b = S.b`, the level `M = S.M`, the

* `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`: the standing hypotheses on `S`, among them `1 ≤ |S.realM v| ≤ b ^ 23`
  and `N ≤ b ^ (60 n)`.
* `New.ψf E`, written `ψ_f`: the character of the finite adeles with `ψ_f(x) = exp (2πi Tr a)` for
  any `a ∈ E` with `x - a` integral. `New.stdAddChar E` is the standard character of the adeles, and
  `New.Filling.selfDualChar` is `x ↦ ψ_f(-x / ϖ)`.

* `New.SieveSystem`: the axioms of the sieve for a family of forms `J i` on pairs of heads, at a

modules.literature:
A system of positive kernels, of one kind at archimedean and finite places, has each kernel the
integral of the next over a common last entry. Systems multiply over places, and one-sided Poisson
summation, entry by entry, bounds the sum over rational points by the mass times a factor near 1, up
to the constants of summation and a small error, as the main term of the second moment requires.
Inductive Fourier transforms of Kloosterman integrals and spectral large sieves losing a constant or
X^ε are known in the literature. Related work: Jacquet, Smooth transfer of Kloosterman integrals,
2003; Jacquet, Kloosterman identities over a quadratic extension, 2004; Blomer–Buttcane, Global
decomposition of GL(3) Kloosterman sums and the spectral large sieve, 2015; Deshouillers–Iwaniec,
Kloosterman sums and Fourier coefficients of cusp forms, 1982.

modules.title: The place and level of a set of primes, orbit sums and the set of entries
modules.note:
This file sets up the local theory at a finite set `T` of finite places, stable under conjugation.
It defines the projection `New.Filling.toPlaces` of the finite adelic unitary group to `T` and the
condition `New.Filling.IsIntegralOff` of being integral off `T`. It also defines the orbit sums
`New.Filling.cosetAmplitude`, the finite set `New.Filling.entrySet` of entries and the condition
`New.Filling.IsFillingData`. It shows that the product `New.LocProd T` of the completions at `T` is
a finite place that carries such a datum.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.exists_isIntegralOff_toPlaces_eq`: every point of the unitary group at `T` is the
  projection of a finite adelic point that is integral off `T`.
* `New.Filling.exists_isFillingData`: `New.LocProd T` is a finite place (`New.Floors.IntegralPlace`)
  with a place datum satisfying `New.Filling.IsFillingData`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.latticeStabilizer`, `New.Filling.principalLevel`: The group `K` of integral points of
  the finite adelic unitary group, and the kernel `K(M)` of its reduction modulo `M`;
  `New.Floors.PlaceData.congruenceSubgroup` is the group `K(M)` at `T`.
* `New.Filling.amplitude`: The integral of β_c(y) β_c'(γ⁻¹y) W(y) ⊗ W(γ⁻¹y)^* over the infinite
  points y, with β_c the cutoff `New.Filling.classCutoff` and W the full or the cut Bessel function
  at infinity, according to the argument `side`.

modules.title: Class sums as orbit sums, and unfolding at a set of primes
modules.note:
This file links the global sums of the filling argument to the local theory at a finite set `T` of
finite places, stable under conjugation. A finite adelic point is studied through its projection
`New.Filling.toPlaces` to `T` and the condition `New.Filling.IsIntegralOff` of being integral off
`T`. This file writes a class sum as a finite sum of orbit sums over the terms in the big cell. It
compares levels, moduli and characters with those at `T`, and it counts images modulo `M` by
measures. It unfolds each orbit sum to a Kloosterman sum at `T` times an orbital integral at
infinity.

With `h_c` the representative `New.Filling.classRep c` of the class `c`,
`New.Filling.translateByClassReps c c' γ` is `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'`, `New.Filling.termsOver c s c'` the set
of rational `γ` for which it is integral of reduction `s` modulo `M`, and
`New.Floors.FloorGroups.weylElem ϱ p` the Weyl element `w_p`. `New.Filling.boundedNonzeroIntegers`
is the finite set of bounded nonzero integers that contains the nonzero leading minors of
contributing terms. `New.Filling.entrySet` is the set 𝒯 of quotients of two of its elements. The
number `New.Filling.termDisc γ` is formed from the last two leading minors of the frame products of
`γ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.exists_amplitudeSum_eq_sum_cosetAmplitude`: a class sum for the cut function is a
  finite sum over the heads with entries in the finite set `New.Filling.entrySet`. Let these entries
  be units off `T` and let all terms over `(c, s, c')` lie in the big cell. If the terms with
  `termDisc γ ≠ 0` and one link have a nonzero sum, those that contribute lie in the double cosets
  of the `w_p σ` for one `σ`. These cosets carry the orbit sums `New.Filling.cosetAmplitude`, over
  the `u γ u'⁻¹` with `u`, `u'` in the unipotent group `New.Shape.Form.besselU`.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.card_reducedImage_mul_measure_congruenceSubgroup_eq`: let `B` be a
  subgroup of the finite adelic group and `μ` an s-finite measure at `T`, carried by the projections
  of elements of `B` integral off `T` and right invariant under the projections of `B`. Then the
  order of the image of `B ∩ K` modulo `M` times `μ K(M)` is the `μ`-measure of the integral points.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.cosetAmplitude_eq_kloostermanSum_smul`: for `γ = w_p σ` with
  `σ ∈ floorGroup ϱ`, and with `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'` and the inverses of the entries of `p` integral off
  `T`, the orbit sum is a Kloosterman sum at `T` times an orbital integral at infinity. Each double
  coset unfolds to one integral, the double cosets correspond to the pairs in the Kloosterman sum,
  and the values of the extended Bessel character are its terms.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.scaledOrbitalIntegral_smul_eq_cosetAmplitude`: so the orbit sum times
  `headDensity` and the mass of `K(M)` is an entry of the integral at `T` times the integral at
  infinity.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.latticeStabilizer`, `New.Filling.principalLevel`: The group `K` of integral points of
  the finite adelic unitary group, and the kernel `K(M)` of its reduction modulo `M`;
  `New.Floors.PlaceData.congruenceSubgroup` is the group `K(M)` at `T`.
* `New.Filling.amplitude`: The integral of β_c(y) β_c'(γ⁻¹y) W(y) ⊗ W(γ⁻¹y)^* over the infinite
  points y, with β_c the cutoff `New.Filling.classCutoff` and W the full or the cut Bessel function
  at infinity, according to the argument `side`.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.extendedBesselChar`: The finite Bessel function, a character of u on u
  K(M) for u in 𝖴 = `New.Shape.Form.besselU`, and 0 off 𝖴 K(M).
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData` (in `New.Spanning.MainTerm.FillingLevel`): the place data at `T` is

* `New.Filling.cosetAmplitude` (in `New.Spanning.MainTerm.FillingLevel`): the sum of the amplitudes

modules.title: Siegel's formula as an upper bound, and domination of class sums by the density at the last entry
modules.note:
Finite-place estimate of the filling theorem: global sums are bounded by integrals over the product
of the completions at a finite set `T` of places, stable under conjugation.

* `New.Filling.adelicFrequency`, `New.Filling.localFrequency`: passage between skew-adjoint
  frequencies at `T` and self-adjoint finite adeles, through multiplication by `-ϖ⁻¹` and `-ϖ`,
  where `ϖ = S.deltaE` generates the different.
* `New.Filling.normDensity_indicator_eq_mul`: the density of a test function that is `Ψ` at `T` and
  the indicator of the lattice off `T` splits into an integral of Gauss sums of the lattice and the
  density of `Ψ` at `T`.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.enorm_normDensity_le_mul_lintegral_normFiberMeasure`: this density is
  at most `1 + b⁻⁶` times the volume of the lattice times the integral of `Ψ` over the sphere of `β`
  at `T`.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.siegel_sum_le_lintegral_sphere`: Siegel's formula bounds the sum of a
  step function over rational points with last entry `t` by a constant times its integral over the
  sphere of `t`.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.exists_step_sum_fiberPairing`: for any matrix `R`, the positive part of
  the real part of the sum of the fiber pairings against `R` is, on the top quadric, the restriction
  of a compactly supported invariant step function.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.sum_mul_norm_sum_cosetAmplitude_sq_le_lastEntryDensity`: the squared
  norms of class sums with one last entry `t` are bounded by `(1 + b⁻⁶) * S.scaledSiegelConst` times
  archimedean densities and densities at `T`, divided by the normalized mass.

The `IsFillingData` results assume `S` admissible, `S.ideleM⁻¹` integral off `T` and `F` filling
data. Conventions: `Φ v` is the embedding of the CM type at `v`. The last entry of `γ` is the
product of the last frame vector with its image under `γ`.
